definition_zh: 加法；增添；新增的人或物；（建筑的）扩建部分
definition_en: the act of putting something together with something already there, or the thing so added
core_image: 一排积木被一块块并到原有的一排上，整排越来越长，桌面还是那张桌面
scene: 仓库管理员把新到的木箱并到原来的货堆上，登记簿上的件数随之变大。Each addition to the stack was recorded in the ledger.
sceneCN: 这里指「并入原有货堆的那一件新东西」（第 3 个义项：新增的人或物）；句意为每往货堆上加一件，都要在登记簿上记下来。可辨识物件：木箱、货堆、登记簿、铅笔。

pos.zh: 加法；增添；新增的人或物；扩建部分

senses.title: Putting numbers together
senses.definition: the arithmetic operation of combining two or more numbers into a single total
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多个数合成一个总数的算术运算
senses.example: Children usually learn addition before multiplication.
senses.exampleCN: 儿童通常先学加法，再学乘法。
senses.why: The Latin verb addere means 'to give to', and arithmetic simply gives one quantity to another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「给到」，算术只是把一个数量给到另一个数量上。

senses.title: Adding something to a whole
senses.definition: the act of joining something to an existing group, amount or structure
senses.definitionCN: 把某物并入已有的群体、数量或结构中的动作
senses.example: The addition of a second engine doubled the ship's speed.
senses.exampleCN: 加装第二台发动机使这艘船的速度翻了一倍。
senses.why: The general sense is older than the arithmetic label: anything given to a whole is an addition.
senses.whyCN: 一般义比算术名称更早：凡是给到整体中去的东西，都是一次增添。

senses.title: A person or thing added
senses.definition: a person or thing that is joined to an existing group
senses.definitionCN: 被并入现有群体的人或物
senses.example: The new goalkeeper proved a valuable addition to the squad.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的守门员成了队里宝贵的新成员。
senses.why: English turns the act into a countable noun, so the thing added is itself called an addition.
senses.whyCN: 英语把这个动作变成可数名词，于是被加进去的东西本身也叫「增添物」。

senses.title: An extension to a building
senses.definition: a part built onto an existing structure
senses.definitionCN: 在已有建筑上接建出来的部分
senses.example: They built a small addition at the back of the house.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在房子后面接建了一个小间。
senses.why: A room joined to a house is the same gesture done in stone and timber.
senses.whyCN: 把一间房接到房子上，是同一个动作用石头和木料做出来。

senses.title: A supplementary clause
senses.definition: something extra attached to a document, contract or list
senses.definitionCN: 附在文件、合同或清单之后的额外内容
senses.example: Two additions were made to the lease before signing.
senses.exampleCN: 签约之前，租约上又添了两条补充条款。
senses.why: Paperwork grows by the same gesture, one item joined to the body of the text.
senses.whyCN: 文书也按同一个动作增长：把一项内容接到正文之后。

senses.title: A chemical addition reaction
senses.definition: a reaction in which one molecule joins another across a double or triple bond
senses.definitionCN: 一个分子加到另一个分子的双键或三键上发生的反应
senses.example: Hydrogen undergoes addition to the double bond under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 在加压条件下，氢加到双键上发生加成。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the everyday word because atoms are literally added across a bond.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用这个日常词，因为原子确实是加到一根键的两端。

senses.title: A further point in an argument
senses.definition: an extra remark or item introduced after what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 在已说内容之后又引入的补充说法或条目
senses.example: In addition, the report notes a fall in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 此外，报告还指出需求有所下降。
senses.why: The fixed phrase marks a new item given to the argument, the same gesture in discourse.
senses.whyCN: 这个固定说法标出给论证新添的一项，是同一个动作在话语中的形态。

senses.title: Cumulative gain
senses.titleCN: 抽象：不断累加形成的增益
senses.definition: the gain that comes from joining many small contributions into one body
senses.definitionCN: 把许多细小贡献并成一个整体所带来的增益
senses.example: The final design is the addition of a hundred small improvements.
senses.exampleCN: 最终设计是一百处小改进叠加起来的产物。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps only the shape of the gesture: many separate pieces becoming one larger thing.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留动作的形状：许多分开的碎片变成一个更大的东西。

intro.en: Addition comes through Old French from Latin additio, a noun built on addere 'to give to', itself ad- 'to, toward' plus dare 'to give'. The deeper root is a reconstruction.
intro.cn: addition 经古法语来自拉丁名词 additio，出自动词 addere「给到」，即 ad-「朝向」加 dare「给」；更早的词根属重构形式。

items.en: Dare means 'to give'. Its earlier root is reconstructed as a verb of giving, the same stock seen in Greek didonai; the reconstruction is conventional rather than attested in writing.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」。其更早的词根被重构为一个表示「给」的动词，与希腊语 didonai 同出一系；这一重构是学界惯例，并非有文字实证。

items.en: Ad- 'toward' plus dare produced addere 'to give to, to join to', the verb behind the whole English family.
items.cn: ad-「朝向」加 dare 构成 addere「给到、接到」，是整个英语词族的动词来源。

items.en: The noun additio named the act of giving something to a whole; it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: 名词 additio 指把某物给到整体中的动作，是英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French addicion carried the word into Middle English in the fourteenth century, first as a general term for anything joined on.
items.cn: 古法语 addicion 在十四世纪把这个词带入中古英语，最初泛指任何接加上去的东西。

items.en: The arithmetic use is old in English, but for centuries the general sense of joining remained the wider one.
items.cn: 算术用法在英语中很早就有，但数个世纪里，「接合」的一般义仍是更宽的用法。

items.en: The building extension and the chemical reaction sense are later specialisations; the chemistry term dates from the nineteenth century, and exact first citations for either are approximate.
items.cn: 建筑扩建义与化学反应义都是后来的专门化；化学术语始于十九世纪，两者的确切首见年代均只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the Latin giving root but differ in prefix or ending; group two holds words for making something larger or longer.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「给」这一词根、但前缀或词尾不同的词；第二组是表示「使变大、使变长」的近义词。

entries.definition: A Latin form of addere meaning 'that which is to be added'; it names a supplement printed at the end of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 这是 addere 的拉丁分词形式，意为「待添入者」；指印在书末的补遗。

entries.definition: From e- 'out' plus dare 'give': a giving out, hence a published version; the resemblance to addition sits in the ending only.
entries.definitionCN: 由 e-「向外」加 dare「给」构成，意为「给出」，引申为出版版本；与 addition 的相似只在词尾。

entries.definition: From ad- plus dicere 'say, declare': originally a person formally assigned to another, with no giving involved.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ad- 加 dicere「说、宣告」构成，原指被正式判归他人的人，与「给」无关。

entries.definition: From ad- plus a verb related to directus 'straight'; it shares the prefix but not the root of addition.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ad- 加一个与 directus「直的」相关的动词构成，只共用前缀，词根不同。

entries.definition: To make an amount or number larger; it says nothing about joining a separate piece.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量或数目变大；不涉及把单独一件东西并进来。

entries.definition: Something added in order to fill a gap or complete a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 为补足缺口或使整体完整而添加的东西。

entries.definition: A part that makes something longer, used of buildings, deadlines and cables.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变长的部分，多用于建筑、期限与线缆。

entries.definition: To place something inside something else, with no suggestion of joining a total.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放进另一物内部，不含有「并入总数」之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'toward' and the root means 'give': giving something to a place is adding it.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「朝向」，词根意为「给」：把东西给到一处，就是增添。

normal.en: One family runs add, addition, additional, additionally, additive and addend.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：加、增添、附加的、此外、添加剂、加数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the main uses: an addition to something, in addition, in addition to.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出主要用法：对某物的增添、此外、除某物之外。

normal.en: The total is called a sum, but the act of reaching it is called addition; keep the two apart.
normal.cn: 加出来的结果叫「和」，而加这个动作叫「加法」，两者要分开。

normal.en: Chemistry names an addition reaction because atoms truly join onto a bond.
normal.cn: 化学把原子加到键上的反应叫加成，正因为原子确实并了上去。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that grows wider as each brick is laid onto it, while the ground below stays the same.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙随着每块砖被砌上去而变宽，而下面的地基始终不变。

abstract.en: Picture a contract that grows thicker as each new clause is attached to the back.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同随着每条新条款贴到后面而越来越厚。

abstract.en: Picture a hundred small improvements merging into one design that no single change explains.
abstract.cn: 想象一百处小改进并成一个设计，没有哪一处改动能单独解释它。

examples.en: The addition of lime to the soil raised its pH.
examples.cn: 往土壤里加石灰提高了它的酸碱度。

examples.en: She is a welcome addition to the research team.
examples.cn: 她是研究团队里受欢迎的新成员。

examples.en: In addition to the fee, students pay for their own materials.
examples.cn: 除了学费之外，学生还要自付材料费。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前缀意为「朝向」，词根意为「给」：把东西给到一处，就是增添；再接上表示动作或结果的名词后缀，就成了「增添」这件事。

root: 拉丁 addere「加上去」＝ ad-（朝向）＋ dare「给」，名词 additio「增添」；dare 更早的来源属重构形式。英语经古法语传入。同族的 addendum 亦出 addere，而「版本」与「沉迷者」两词虽形近，前缀或词根并不相同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is given to something already there, and that movement is then read as arithmetic, as a new member, as a wing of a house, as a clause, as a chemical bond, and finally as the quiet gain of many small pieces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把某物给到已经在那里的东西上，这个动作再依次读作算术、新成员、房屋的接建、条款、化学键，最后读作许多小片并成的静默增益。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall that grows wider as each new brick is laid onto the row already there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面墙随着每块新砖砌到已有的那一排上而变宽。

branches.en: GIVE TO: arithmetic and the addition reaction both give one unit to another along a bond or a column.
branches.cn: 给到：算术与加成反应都是把一个单位沿一条键或一列数字给到另一个单位。

branches.en: JOIN ON: the act and the thing joined are the same gesture seen from two sides.
branches.cn: 接上：动作与被接上的东西是同一动作的两面。

branches.en: EXTRA ROOM: a wing is the gesture done in stone and timber.
branches.cn: 多出的房间：接建的部分是同一动作用石头和木料做出来。

branches.en: EXTRA CLAUSE: paper and speech grow by one item attached at the end.
branches.cn: 追加条款：文书与话语都靠末尾接上的一项而增长。

branches.en: SMALL GAINS: the abstract sense keeps only the shape, many pieces becoming one larger body.
branches.cn: 小增益：抽象义只保留形状，即许多碎片变成一个更大的整体。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb plus a noun ending, and both parts also build several English words, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁动词加名词词尾构成，两部分还构成若干英语词，因此整个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin dare 'to give' yields addere, additio and additamentum; the prefix ad- adds direction toward something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dare「给」衍生出 addere、additio 与 additamentum；前缀 ad- 增添「朝向某物」的方向。

items.example: The prefix turns the action toward its object.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作指向它的对象。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of handing something over.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「把东西交出去」的意思。

items.example: The Latin verb adds direction to the act of giving.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词给「给」这个动作加上了方向。

items.meaning: to join one thing to another
items.example: Add the figures in the last column.
items.exampleCN: 把最后一列的数字加起来。

items.meaning: the act or result of adding
items.example: The addition took two minutes.
items.exampleCN: 这次相加花了两分钟。

items.example: An additional charge applies after midnight.
items.exampleCN: 午夜之后另收附加费。

items.example: Additionally, the room faces south.
items.exampleCN: 此外，这间房朝南。

items.structure: add + -itive (noun or adjective suffix, tending to)
items.meaning: a substance added; relating to addition
items.example: The fuel contains a cleaning additive.
items.exampleCN: 这种燃料含有清洁添加剂。

latinEntries.meaning: that which is added, a supplement

definition_zh: 减去；扣除；使减少；从整体中抽走
definition_en: to take one quantity away from another, or to remove a part from a whole
core_image: 一筐果子被逐个数出去，筐里变少，桌面上那堆变多
scene: 会计在核对账目时把已付的定金从总额里划掉。She subtracted the deposit from the final bill.
sceneCN: 这里指「从总额中扣除已付的部分」（第 2 个义项：从款项中扣除）；句意为她把定金从最终账单里扣掉。可辨识物件：账单、计算器、笔、对账清单。

senses.title: Take one number from another
senses.titleCN: 从一个数里减去另一个数
senses.definition: to take a number or quantity away from a larger one in arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 在算术中从较大的数里拿走一个数或量
senses.example: Subtract seven from twenty and you get thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 从二十里减去七，得到十三。
senses.why: Latin sub- 'from below' plus trahere 'draw' pictures pulling a quantity out from under the total.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 sub-「从下面」加 trahere「拉」构成一幅画面：把一份量从总数底下抽走。

senses.title: Deduct an amount from a bill
senses.definition: to take a charge or payment away from an amount owed
senses.definitionCN: 从应付金额中减去某项费用或已付款项
senses.example: The bank subtracts its fee before crediting the interest.
senses.exampleCN: 银行先扣掉手续费，再把利息记入账户。
senses.why: Money is drawn off before the remainder is credited, exactly the Latin image of pulling something away.
senses.whyCN: 先把钱抽走再记入余款，正是拉丁语「抽走」那幅画面。

senses.title: Remove a part from a whole
senses.definition: to take a physical part out of a larger object or set
senses.definitionCN: 从较大的物体或集合中取出一个实体部分
senses.example: Workers subtracted several damaged beams from the shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 工人从这批货里抽出了几根损坏的横梁。
senses.why: The arithmetic sense grew out of this plain physical removal, with counting added later.
senses.whyCN: 算术义由这种朴素的物理取出发展而来，计数是后来才加上的。

senses.title: Detract from a quality
senses.definition: to make something less valuable or less convincing
senses.definitionCN: 使某物的价值或说服力降低
senses.example: A single error can subtract from an otherwise strong argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一个错误就能削弱一个本来有力的论证。
senses.why: The Latin image is pulling something away; a quality can be pulled away in the same way, leaving the whole poorer.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的形象是抽走东西；质量也能这样被抽走，使整体变得贫乏。

senses.title: Work out a net figure
senses.definition: to remove costs or losses in order to reach a net amount
senses.definitionCN: 去掉成本或损失以得到净额
senses.example: Subtract costs from revenue to find the margin.
senses.exampleCN: 从收入里减去成本，就能得出利润率。
senses.why: Accounting keeps the literal sense: the gross figure has something drawn out of it.
senses.whyCN: 会计保留了字面义：总额里被抽走了一部分。

senses.title: Exclude a group from a count
senses.definition: to leave a category out of a total before counting
senses.definitionCN: 计数之前先把某一类排除在总数之外
senses.example: Surveys often subtract visitors who stay less than a day.
senses.exampleCN: 调查常常把停留不足一天的访客排除在外。
senses.why: The gesture moves from objects to categories: a whole class is drawn off before the sum is taken.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作从实物转到类别：在求和之前把整类抽走。

senses.title: Cut a score by a penalty
senses.definition: to reduce a score by a stated penalty
senses.definitionCN: 按规定的罚则降低得分
senses.example: The judges subtracted two points for the late start.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判因开场延迟扣了两分。
senses.why: A penalty is a fixed amount pulled off a total, so the arithmetic sense fits without change.
senses.whyCN: 罚分是从总数里抽走的固定量，算术义不用改动就能套用。

senses.title: Strip away the inessential
senses.definition: to remove whatever is not necessary until only the essential remains
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一切不必要的东西，直到只剩本质
senses.example: Good design subtracts until only the necessary remains.
senses.exampleCN: 好的设计不断做减法，直到只剩必要之物。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the gesture with no numbers left: whatever is inessential is drawn off.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了这个动作，只是不再有数字：凡非本质的都被抽走。

intro.en: Subtract comes from Latin subtractus, the past participle of subtrahere 'to draw away', built on sub- 'from below' and trahere 'to draw, pull'. Beyond Latin the origin of trahere is unsettled.
intro.cn: subtract 出自拉丁 subtractus，即 subtrahere「抽走」的过去分词，由 sub-「从下面」与 trahere「拉、拖」构成；trahere 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, pull, drag'. Its deeper origin is not established, so any older root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、拽」。其更早来源未得到证明，凡为其拟出的更古老词根都属重构形式。

items.en: Sub- 'under, from below' plus trahere produced subtrahere 'to draw away, withdraw'.
items.cn: sub-「在下、从下面」加 trahere 构成 subtrahere「抽走、撤回」。

items.en: The participle subtractus supplied both the English verb and the noun subtraction.
items.cn: 分词 subtractus 同时提供了英语动词与名词 subtraction。

items.en: Old French versions of the verb passed into English in the fifteenth century, at first in general use rather than as a schoolroom term.
items.cn: 该动词的古法语形式在十五世纪进入英语，起初是一般用法，而非课堂术语。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word was fixed as the ordinary term for taking one number from another.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词已固定为「从一个数里减去另一个数」的通常说法。

items.en: The sense of taking away value or quality developed alongside the arithmetic one; the penalty sense is a late extension of counting.
items.cn: 「取走价值或质量」的用法与算术义并行发展；扣分义是计数用法的较晚延伸。

note.en: Group one gathers verbs built on Latin trahere with different prefixes, which is why they look alike; group two gathers ordinary words for taking something away.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 trahere、但前缀不同的动词，因此形貌相近；第二组是表示「拿走」的普通近义词。

entries.definition: Abs- 'away' plus trahere: to draw something out of its setting, hence to abstract an idea.
entries.definitionCN: abs-「离开」加 trahere：把某物从原有情境中抽出，故指抽象出观念。

entries.definition: Con- 'together' plus trahere: to draw parts together, hence to shrink; the legal document is a separate development.
entries.definitionCN: con-「一起」加 trahere：把各部分拉到一起，故指收缩；合同义是另一条发展线。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus trahere: to pull something out, as a tooth or a passage from a text.
entries.definitionCN: ex-「向外」加 trahere：把某物拉出来，如拔牙或摘录一段文字。

entries.definition: Dis- 'apart' plus trahere: to pull attention away in different directions.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 trahere：把注意力往不同方向拉开。

entries.definition: To take a fixed sum off an amount, used mostly of money, tax or points.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个数额中按规定减掉一笔，多用于钱、税或分数。

entries.definition: To move something out of its place; it says nothing about numbers.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物从原位移走；完全不涉及数字。

entries.definition: To reduce a price, or to treat a claim as not worth counting.
entries.definitionCN: 降低价格，或认为某种说法不值得计入。

entries.definition: To make something smaller in degree rather than in number.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物在程度上变小，而不是在数量上减少。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'from below' and the root means 'draw': drawing a number out from under the total is subtraction.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「从下面」，词根意为「拉」：把数字从总数底下拉出来，就是减。

normal.en: One family runs subtract, subtraction, subtractive, subtrahend and subtracter.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：减去、减法、减去的、减数、做减法者。

normal.en: All five verbs on the same root differ only by prefix: pull away, together, out, apart and from below.
normal.cn: 同根的那几个动词只靠前缀区别：拉走、拉拢、拉出、拉开、从底下拉。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the accounting use: subtract costs, subtract tax, subtract the difference.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出记账用法：扣除成本、扣除税款、减去差额。

normal.en: The number taken away has its own name, the subtrahend, which is the Latin word for 'to be subtracted'.
normal.cn: 被拿走的那个数有专名，即「减数」，字面就是拉丁语「待减去者」。

abstract.en: Picture a sack of grain that lightens as each scoop is taken out and piled beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一袋粮食随着每勺被舀出并堆在旁边而变轻。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures with one line ruled through, the line then reappearing at the bottom as a smaller total.
abstract.cn: 想象一列数字中被划掉一行，那一行随后在底部以更小的总数重新出现。

abstract.en: Picture a sculptor cutting away marble until only the shape that was hidden remains.
abstract.cn: 想象雕刻家不断凿去大理石，直到只剩原本藏在里面的形状。

examples.en: Subtract the smaller reading from the larger one.
examples.cn: 用较大的读数减去较小的读数。

examples.en: Late penalties are subtracted from the final payment.
examples.cn: 滞纳罚金会从最终付款中扣除。

examples.en: One rude remark can subtract from an hour of careful explanation.
examples.cn: 一句粗鲁的话就能削弱一小时耐心解释的效果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前缀意为「从下面」，词根意为「拉」：把一份量从总数底下拉走，就是减去；拉走的那一份在账上要扣掉。

root: 拉丁 subtrahere「抽走」＝ sub-（从下面）＋ trahere「拉、拖」，过去分词 subtractus 派生英语动词与名词；trahere 更早来源无定论。同根诸词 abstract、contract、extract、distract（拉走、拉拢、拉出、拉开）只靠前缀区分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a part is drawn out of a whole. Arithmetic counts the drawn part, accounting prices it, grammar makes it a penalty, and the abstract sense draws off whatever is not needed.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一部分从整体里抽走。算术为抽走的部分计数，会计为它定价，规则把它变成罚分，抽象义则抽走一切不必要之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pulls one scoop of grain out of a full sack and sets it aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手从满袋粮食里舀出一勺，放到旁边。

branches.en: DRAW OUT: counting and physical removal are one gesture, one with numbers and one with objects.
branches.cn: 抽出：计数与实物取出是同一个动作，一个带数字，一个带实物。

branches.en: MONEY: a charge or cost is drawn off before the net figure is named.
branches.cn: 钱款：在说出净额之前先抽走一项费用或成本。

branches.en: QUALITY: value and persuasiveness can be pulled away like grain from a sack.
branches.cn: 质量：价值与说服力也像袋里的粮食一样能被抽走。

branches.en: COUNTING RULES: a category or a penalty is a fixed amount removed before the total is read.
branches.cn: 计数规则：一整类人或一笔罚分，都是在读总数之前先减掉的定量。

branches.en: STRIP AWAY: with no numbers left, the gesture becomes the removal of the unnecessary.
branches.cn: 剥离：不再有数字时，这个动作就变成去掉不必要之物。

intro.en: Subtract is a Latin verb whose prefix and root both recur in English, which is why a whole set of look-alike verbs can be sorted by prefix alone.
intro.cn: subtract 是一个拉丁动词，前缀与词根都在英语中反复出现，因此一整组形近动词可以只按前缀归类。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere gives subtract, abstract, contract, extract and distract; sub- adds the direction 'from below'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 trahere 衍生 subtract、abstract、contract、extract、distract；sub- 增添「从下面」的方向。

items.example: The prefix places the action beneath the whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放到整体之下。

items.example: The root carries the image of dragging something out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着「把东西拖出来」的形象。

items.example: The Latin verb joins direction to the act of pulling.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词把方向与「拉」的动作结合起来。

items.meaning: to take one quantity from another
items.example: Subtract the fee from the total.
items.exampleCN: 从总额中扣掉这笔费用。

items.meaning: the act or result of taking away
items.example: Subtraction is the inverse of addition.
items.exampleCN: 减法是加法的逆运算。

items.example: The process is subtractive rather than additive.
items.exampleCN: 这个过程是减法式的，而非加法式的。

items.meaning: the number that is to be subtracted
items.example: In ten minus four, four is the subtrahend.
items.exampleCN: 十减四中，四就是减数。

items.example: The circuit contains a binary subtracter.
items.exampleCN: 这个电路里有一个二进制减法器。

latinEntries.meaning: that which is to be subtracted

definition_zh: 减法；减法运算过程；扣除额；减少
definition_en: the arithmetic operation of taking one quantity away from another, or the amount so taken

sceneCN: 这里指「减法这项运算本身」（第 1 个义项：减法运算）；句意为全班练习三位数的减法。可辨识物件：黑板、粉笔、竖式、横线。

pos.zh: 减法；扣除；减少；被减去的量

collocations.phrase: subtraction of one number from another
collocations.zh: 用一个数减去另一个数

senses.title: The arithmetic operation
senses.definition: the operation of taking one number away from another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个数里拿走另一个数的运算
senses.example: Subtraction is taught alongside addition in the first year.
senses.exampleCN: 减法在一年级就与加法一起教。
senses.why: The noun names the operation itself, built directly on the Latin verb for drawing away.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接由拉丁动词「抽走」构成，指运算本身。

senses.title: The working of such a problem
senses.definition: the written or mental working by which such a problem is solved
senses.definitionCN: 解这类题时写出来或心算的过程
senses.example: Her subtraction was neat, with every borrow marked.
senses.exampleCN: 她的减法写得整齐，每次借位都标了出来。
senses.why: English lets the name of the operation also cover the steps taken to carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 英语让运算的名称同时覆盖执行它的步骤。

senses.title: The amount taken away
senses.definition: the quantity that is removed from a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 从较大量中取走的那份量
senses.example: The subtraction from the budget was larger than expected.
senses.exampleCN: 预算被削减的数额比预期更大。
senses.why: The same noun serves for the act and for its result, a pattern English uses constantly.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指动作也指结果，这是英语常见的做法。

senses.title: A reduction in amount
senses.definition: a decrease in an amount, especially one made deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 数量的减少，尤指有意造成的减少
senses.example: A subtraction of ten staff changed the office entirely.
senses.exampleCN: 减掉十名员工让办公室完全变了样。
senses.why: Counting the removed part turns naturally into naming the reduction itself.
senses.whyCN: 为被拿走的部分计数，自然就转为命名这次减少。

senses.title: The minus sign in notation
senses.definition: the sign used to mark this operation in written arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 书面算术中标记这一运算的符号
senses.example: A subtraction sign is a short horizontal stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 减号是一道短短的横线。
senses.why: The sign is called by the name of the operation it performs, a common shorthand in mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 这个符号以它所执行的运算命名，是数学里常见的简写。

senses.title: A deduction in accounts
senses.definition: an item deducted before a balance is struck
senses.definitionCN: 结账之前被扣除的项目
senses.example: The statement lists each subtraction from the gross sum.
senses.exampleCN: 账单把从总额中扣掉的每一项都列了出来。
senses.why: Bookkeeping treats every removal as a named entry, so the operation becomes a line in a ledger.
senses.whyCN: 记账把每次移除都当成一个有名字的条目，于是运算变成账簿上的一行。

senses.title: Finding what remains by exclusion
senses.definition: the method of finding what is left by ruling out what it is not
senses.definitionCN: 通过排除「不是什么」来求出剩下的是什么
senses.example: The detective worked by subtraction, discarding every impossible route.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探用排除法，把每条不可能的路都划掉。
senses.why: The metaphor extends the arithmetic: whatever is ruled out is taken away until one answer remains.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻把算术延伸开：凡被排除的都被拿走，直到只剩一个答案。

senses.title: Stripping away the unnecessary
senses.definition: the act of removing whatever is not essential
senses.definitionCN: 去掉一切非必要成分的行为
senses.example: The final edit was pure subtraction, cutting every line that repeated the point.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一轮修改纯粹是做减法，删掉了每一句重复的话。
senses.why: With numbers gone, subtraction becomes the discipline of taking away rather than the count of what is left.
senses.whyCN: 数字消失之后，减法变成「取走」的自律，而不是对剩余之物的计数。

intro.en: Subtraction comes from Late Latin subtractio, a noun of action from subtrahere 'to draw away'. The verb is sub- 'from below' plus trahere 'to draw'; the earlier origin of trahere is unsettled.
intro.cn: subtraction 出自晚期拉丁名词 subtractio，是 subtrahere「抽走」的动作名词；该动词由 sub-「从下面」加 trahere「拉」构成，trahere 的更早来源无定论。

items.en: Trahere meant 'to draw, pull'. Its pre-Latin origin is not established, so any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖」。它在拉丁语之前的来源未获证明，凡为其引出的更古老形式都属重构形式。

items.en: Sub- 'from below' plus trahere gave subtrahere 'to draw away, take away'.
items.cn: sub-「从下面」加 trahere 得出 subtrahere「抽走、拿走」。

items.en: The action noun subtractio named the drawing away itself; English took the noun rather than the Latin verb form.
items.cn: 动作名词 subtractio 指「抽走」这件事本身；英语取的是这个名词，而非拉丁动词原形。

items.en: The noun appeared in English in the fifteenth century, at first in general use and only later as a school term.
items.cn: 这个名词在十五世纪进入英语，起初是一般用法，后来才成为课堂术语。

items.en: Printing and schooling fixed subtraction as the standard name of the operation from the seventeenth century onward.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，印刷与学校教育使 subtraction 固定为这项运算的标准名称。

items.en: The figurative sense of ruling things out till one answer remains is modern and rests on the arithmetic image.
items.cn: 「不断排除直到只剩一个答案」的比喻用法属现代发展，依托于算术形象。

note.en: Group one holds words that wear the same noun ending or come from the same verb; group two holds words for a decrease or a deduction.
note.cn: 第一组是共用同一名词词尾、或出自同一动词的词；第二组是表示「减少」或「扣除」的近义词。

entries.definition: The inverse operation, built on a different Latin verb; the matching ending hides a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 与之相反的运算，出自另一个拉丁动词；相同的词尾掩盖了不同的词根。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed; the noun names the operation, the verb the act.
entries.definitionCN: 名词由这个动词构成；名词指运算，动词指动作。

entries.definition: The technical name for the quantity taken away, from the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 被取走那个量的专门名称，出自同一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: From de- plus ducere 'lead': a leading away, hence an amount deducted; the ending matches but the root does not.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de- 加 ducere「引导」构成，意为「引走」，引申为扣除额；词尾相同而词根不同。

entries.definition: A general word for making an amount smaller, whether by taking away or by lowering a rate.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量变小的通称，无论靠拿走一部分还是靠降低比率。

entries.definition: To become or make less, used of sizes, rates and numbers without any arithmetic frame.
entries.definitionCN: 变小或使变小，用于尺寸、比率与数量，不带算术框架。

entries.definition: The act of moving something out of its place, usually physical.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物移出原位的动作，通常指实物。

entries.definition: An informal word for a reduction ordered by someone, as in a cut in funding.
entries.definitionCN: 由某方决定削减的口语说法，如削减经费。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The noun is the verb plus an action ending, so it names the operation rather than the person doing it.
normal.cn: 名词由动词加动作词尾构成，因此它指运算，而不是做运算的人。

normal.en: The family runs subtract, subtraction, subtractive, subtrahend and subtractional.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：减去、减法、减去的、减数、减法上的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the classroom: a subtraction problem, a subtraction sign, repeated subtraction.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出课堂场景：减法题、减号、连减。

normal.en: Every word built on the same root differs by prefix: away, together, out, apart, from below.
normal.cn: 同根词只靠前缀区别：离开、一起、向外、分开、从下面。

normal.en: In a written sum the removed number is the subtrahend, a Latin tag meaning 'to be subtracted'.
normal.cn: 在竖式里被拿走的那个数是「减数」，这个拉丁标签意为「待减去者」。

abstract.en: Picture a blackboard with one line of figures ruled out and a smaller figure written beneath the rule.
abstract.cn: 想象黑板上有一行数字被划掉，横线下面写着一个更小的数。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf from which one book is taken, leaving a gap exactly the size of that book.
abstract.cn: 想象书架上被取走一本书，留下的空当恰好是那本书的大小。

abstract.en: Picture a sculptor's block losing everything that was never part of the figure inside.
abstract.cn: 想象雕刻的石块失去了一切从来不属于里面那个人形的部分。

examples.en: The worksheet mixes addition and subtraction.
examples.cn: 这张练习纸把加法与减法混在一起。

examples.en: Repeated subtraction is one way to introduce division.
examples.cn: 连减是引入除法的一种方式。

examples.en: The subtraction of two senior posts left the team short of experience.
examples.cn: 撤掉两个资深岗位使团队缺少经验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词意为「从底下拉走」，加表示动作或结果的名词词尾，就得到「减法」这件事；被拉走的那份量也用同一个词。

root: 拉丁晚期 subtractio「抽走」＝ sub-（从下面）＋ trahere「拉」，动作名词化；trahere 更早来源无定论。同根动词靠前缀分流：abstract 拉走、contract 拉拢、extract 拉出、distract 拉开。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a part is drawn out of a whole. The operation, its written working, the part removed, the reduction, the sign, the ledger line, the detective's method and the editor's cut are all the same drawing-away.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一部分从整体里抽走。运算、竖式过程、被取走的量、数量的减少、运算符号、账上的扣减、侦探的排除法、编者的删削，都是这同一次抽走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rule drawn through one line of figures, leaving a smaller total beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道横线划掉一行数字，线下留下一个更小的总数。

branches.en: THE RULE: the operation and the steps that carry it out share one name.
branches.cn: 规则：运算本身与执行它的步骤共用一个名称。

branches.en: THE PART: what is taken and the resulting reduction are two views of one subtraction.
branches.cn: 部分：被取走的量与由此造成的减少，是同一次减法的两个看法。

branches.en: THE MARK: a short stroke stands for the whole operation.
branches.cn: 标记：一道短横代表整个运算。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: accounts give every removal a line of its own.
branches.cn: 账簿：会计给每一次移除单独列一行。

branches.en: RULING OUT: with no numbers left, subtraction becomes exclusion and then disciplined cutting.
branches.cn: 排除：没有数字之后，减法先变成排除，再变成有纪律的删削。

intro.en: Subtraction is a Latin action noun; its prefix, root and ending each recur across English, so the word repays being read in parts.
intro.cn: subtraction 是一个拉丁动作名词；它的前缀、词根与词尾都在英语中反复出现，因此值得按部分来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin subtrahere yields subtract, subtraction and subtrahend; the ending -io, -ionis becomes English -ion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 subtrahere 衍生 subtract、subtraction 与 subtrahend；词尾 -io、-ionis 在英语中变为 -ion。

items.example: The prefix sets the direction of the removal.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀定出取走的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling gesture.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「拉」的动作。

items.example: The Latin verb is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词是整个词族的基础。

items.structure: English verb from the Latin participle subtractus

items.example: Subtract the fee first.
items.exampleCN: 先扣除费用。

items.meaning: the act or result of drawing away
items.example: Subtraction reverses addition.
items.exampleCN: 减法反转加法。

items.example: The method is subtractive.
items.exampleCN: 这种方法靠逐步去除。

items.example: Name the subtrahend before you work.
items.exampleCN: 动笔前先指出减数。

items.example: A subtractional error changed the answer.
items.exampleCN: 一处减法错误改变了答案。

definition_zh: 总和；金额；概要；算术题；合计；概括
definition_en: the total reached by adding things together, or the act of adding them up
core_image: 一列数字被加到最下面，底部写出一个更大的数，旁边画一道横线
scene: 出纳把几张发票的金额加在一起，在纸上写出总数。The sum of the five invoices was far above the budget.
sceneCN: 这里指「把若干数加在一起得到的总数」（第 1 个义项：数学上的和）；句意为五张发票的金额加起来远超预算。可辨识物件：发票、计算器、铅笔、横线。

senses.title: A total in arithmetic
senses.definition: the total produced by adding two or more numbers
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多个数相加得到的总数
senses.example: The sum of the angles in a triangle is two right angles.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形内角之和等于两个直角。
senses.why: Latin summa was the highest line of a column, where Roman clerks wrote the total, so 'highest' became 'total'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 summa 原指一列数字的最上面一行，罗马书吏把合计写在那里，于是「最高」变成了「总数」。

senses.title: An amount of money
senses.definition: a particular amount of money, especially a large one
senses.definitionCN: 一笔特定数额的钱，尤指较大的数目
senses.example: She paid the full sum in a single transfer.
senses.exampleCN: 她一次性转账付清了全部款项。
senses.why: Money counted into one figure is the same image: a column of amounts closed by a total.
senses.whyCN: 把钱数合成一个数字是同一幅画面：一列金额由合计收尾。

senses.title: The whole of something
senses.definition: the whole of something considered as one quantity
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物当作一个量来看的整体
senses.example: The sum of the evidence points one way.
senses.exampleCN: 全部证据都指向同一个方向。
senses.why: Once a total is named, it can stand for the whole body of things that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 总数一旦被命名，就可以代表产生它的全部内容。

senses.title: A summary in brief
senses.definition: a short statement of the main points of something longer
senses.definitionCN: 对较长内容的主要之点所作的简短陈述
senses.example: In sum, the experiment failed for three reasons.
senses.exampleCN: 总而言之，这个实验失败有三个原因。
senses.why: The total of a speech is its main point, so the word slid from adding figures to gathering arguments.
senses.whyCN: 一篇话的「总数」就是它的要点，于是这个词从加数字滑向收拢论点。

senses.title: To add up to a figure
senses.definition: to reach a stated total when the parts are added
senses.definitionCN: 各部分相加后达到某个总数
senses.example: The parts sum to a total of ninety.
senses.exampleCN: 各部分合计为九十。
senses.why: The verb keeps the arithmetic image and simply states what the column comes to.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留算术形象，只是说明这一列最终等于多少。

senses.title: To gather into a summary
senses.definition: to state the main points of something in a short form
senses.definitionCN: 用简短形式说出某内容的主要之点
senses.example: The chair summed up the argument in two sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 主席用两句话概括了这场论证。
senses.why: Gathering scattered points into one statement is adding again, with ideas instead of figures.
senses.whyCN: 把散落的要点收成一句话，仍是加法，只是用观念代替数字。

senses.title: An arithmetic exercise
senses.definition: a problem in arithmetic, especially one set for practice
senses.definitionCN: 一道算术题，尤指布置来练习的题
senses.example: Pupils still do sums without a calculator.
senses.exampleCN: 小学生仍在不借助计算器做算术题。
senses.why: British usage names the school exercise after the answer it produces, a plain metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 英式用法以答案代指学校练习，是朴素的换喻。

senses.title: The product of many parts
senses.definition: the combined result of many contributions over time
senses.definitionCN: 许多贡献长期累积而成的总体结果
senses.example: The building is the sum of a hundred small decisions.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑是一百个小决定累积成的总体。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops the column and keeps only the shape: many parts closing into one result.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉那一列数字，只保留形状：许多部分收成一个结果。

intro.en: Sum comes from Latin summa, the feminine of summus 'highest', used for the top line of a column of figures where the total was written. The noun reached English through Old French summe.
intro.cn: sum 出自拉丁 summa，是 summus「最高」的阴性形式，罗马人把合计写在一列数字的最上面一行，故用它指总数；该名词经古法语 summe 进入英语。

items.en: Summus was the superlative of superus 'upper', meaning 'highest, topmost'. It regularly described the top position in a column or a list.
items.cn: summus 是 superus「在上」的最高级，意为「最高、最上」，常用来描述一列或一表中的顶端位置。

items.en: Summa, the feminine form used as a noun, meant 'the chief part' and also 'the total', because the total stood at the top of the reckoning.
items.cn: summa 作名词用的阴性形式，意为「主要部分」，也指「总数」，因为合计写在一笔账的最上方。

items.en: The verb summare 'to reckon up, bring to a total' supplied the English verb to sum.
items.cn: 动词 summare「结算、加成总数」提供了英语动词的用法。

items.en: Old French summe carried the noun into Middle English in the thirteenth century, first in the money sense.
items.cn: 古法语 summe 在十三世纪把这个名词带入中古英语，最初用于钱的数目。

items.en: The money sense is medieval; the sense of a brief statement grew from the idea of the total of an argument in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 钱的用法属中世纪；把论证的「总数」说成扼要陈述，这一用法在十六世纪发展出来。

items.en: The British sense of a school arithmetic exercise is a later metonymy and has no exact first date; early citations are approximate.
items.cn: 英式「学校算术题」的用法是较晚的换喻，确切首见年代不明，早期书证只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like sum because they begin with the same letters but come from other verbs; group two holds genuine near-synonyms for a total.
note.cn: 第一组是因开头字母相同而形近、实际出自别的动词的词；第二组是真正表示「总数」的近义词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin summa, by way of the idea of the chief points; it is the abstract of a text, not a total of figures.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 summa，取「主要之点」的意思；指文章的摘要，而非数字的合计。

entries.definition: The act or result of summing, used in mathematics and in argument.
entries.definitionCN: 求和的动作或结果，用于数学与论证。

entries.definition: From ad- plus sumere 'take': to take something for granted; the shared letters belong to another verb entirely.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ad- 加 sumere「拿取」构成，意为「视为当然」；相同的字母来自完全另一个动词。

entries.definition: From com- plus sumere 'take': to take up entirely, hence to use up; it is not related to summa.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com- 加 sumere「拿取」构成，意为「全部取走」，引申为消耗；与 summa 无关。

entries.definition: The whole amount reached by adding; the closest everyday synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 相加得到的全部数量；最接近的日常同义词。

entries.definition: The quantity of something, not necessarily reached by adding.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的数量，不一定由相加得出。

entries.definition: A total formed by collecting many separate items, used in statistics and economics.
entries.definitionCN: 由收集许多单独项而形成的总数，用于统计与经济学。

entries.definition: All the parts taken as one thing, with no arithmetic operation implied.
entries.definitionCN: 把全部部分当作一个整体，不含运算之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Latin noun meant the top line of a reckoning, which is why a total and a summit share a root.
normal.cn: 那个拉丁名词原指一列账的最上面一行，因此「总数」与「顶点」共用一个词根。

normal.en: One family runs sum, summary, summarize, summation and summit.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：总数、摘要、概括、求和、顶点。

normal.en: Fixed phrases carry the main uses: a sum of money, in sum, sum up, a lump sum.
normal.cn: 固定说法承载主要用法：一笔钱、总而言之、概括、整笔付款。

normal.en: The verb is regular: sums, summed, summed, summing.
normal.cn: 动词变化规则：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 sums、summed、summed、summing。

normal.en: Words that merely begin with the same letters, like assume and consume, come from a different Latin verb meaning 'take'.
normal.cn: 只是开头字母相同的词，如假定与消耗，出自另一个意为「拿取」的拉丁动词。

abstract.en: Picture a column of figures on a slate with a line drawn beneath it and one larger number written below the line.
abstract.cn: 想象石板上一列数字，下面画一道横线，线下的位置写着一个更大的数。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of coins merged into one stack whose height nobody can mistake.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆散币被并成一摞，高度一眼就能看出。

abstract.en: Picture a long meeting compressed into one sentence written on a card.
abstract.cn: 想象一场长会被压缩成卡片上的一句话。

examples.en: The sum of the two fractions is less than one.
examples.cn: 这两个分数的和小于一。

examples.en: He left a large sum to the village school.
examples.cn: 他给村里的学校留下了一大笔钱。

examples.en: Sum up the findings in a single paragraph.
examples.cn: 用一段话概括这些发现。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拉丁里「最高的一行」就是账上写合计的地方，于是「最高」转为「总数」；把散落的要点收成一句，也就是概括。

root: 拉丁 summa「总数」原为 summus「最高」的阴性名词，指一列数字顶端写合计的那一行；动词 summare「结算」给出动词义。英语经古法语传入。assume、consume 出自另一动词 sumere「拿取」，与 summa 不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: a column of figures closed by a line and a single total. That total is then read as money, as a whole, as the brief of an argument, as a school exercise, and finally as the shape of many parts becoming one result.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一幅画面展开：一列数字被一道横线收住，写出一个总数。这个总数再依次读作钱、读作整体、读作论证的要点、读作学校练习，最后读作许多部分收成一个结果的形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of figures with a line beneath it and one larger number written below the line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一列数字下面画一道横线，线下写着一个更大的数。

branches.en: TOTAL: the noun names the result, the verb states what the parts come to.
branches.cn: 总数：名词指结果，动词说明各部分最终等于多少。

branches.en: MONEY: amounts of cash are a column closed by a single figure.
branches.cn: 钱：一笔笔款项就是一列由单一数字收住的数。

branches.en: WHOLE: a total can stand for the entire body of things behind it.
branches.cn: 整体：总数可以代表它背后那整批东西。

branches.en: THE POINT: the total of a speech is its main point, gathered in one statement.
branches.cn: 要点：一篇话的总数就是它的要点，收在一句话里。

branches.en: MANY INTO ONE: a school exercise and a lifetime of decisions are both many parts closing into one result.
branches.cn: 多收为一：学校练习与一生的决定，都是许多部分收成一个结果。

intro.en: Sum is a Latin noun of degree that became a noun of quantity; its root also builds words for the top point and for the abstract of a text.
intro.cn: sum 是一个拉丁程度名词，后来变成数量名词；同一词根还构成表示顶点与文章摘要的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin summus and summa yield sum, summary, summation and summit; the ending -ary marks a thing that serves as a chief statement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 summus 与 summa 衍生 sum、summary、summation、summit；词尾 -ary 标记「用作要点之物」。

items.example: The adjective named the top line of a written column.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指书写一列数字时最上面的那一行。

items.example: The noun shifted from position to quantity.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词从位置义转到数量义。

items.example: The verb names the act of reaching the total.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指达成总数的动作。

items.example: The sum came to ninety.
items.exampleCN: 总数达到九十。

items.structure: summa + -ary (noun or adjective suffix, serving as)
items.meaning: a brief statement of the chief points
items.example: The summary runs to one page.
items.exampleCN: 摘要只有一页。

items.example: Summarize the chapter in five lines.
items.exampleCN: 用五行话概括这一章。

items.meaning: the act or result of adding up
items.example: The summation of the series is finite.
items.exampleCN: 这个级数的求和是有限的。

items.meaning: the topmost point; a top-level meeting
items.example: They reached the summit at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时登上顶峰。

definition_zh: 差别；差额；分歧；区别；特色；集合差
definition_en: the way in which two things are not the same, or the amount by which one differs from another
core_image: 两条并排的线各自延伸，中间留下的一道缝就是两者的差
scene: 实验员把两组读数并排贴在记录板上，中间那道缝一眼可见。The difference between the two readings was small but consistent.
sceneCN: 这里指「两个数值之间不一样的地方」（第 1 个义项：差别）；句意为两组读数之间的差别虽小却始终一致。可辨识物件：记录板、读数条、直尺、标记笔。

pos.zh: 差别；差额；分歧；区别；特色

senses.title: The way two things are unlike
senses.definition: the respect in which two things are not the same
senses.definitionCN: 两个事物不一样的那个方面
senses.example: The difference between the twins is easy to miss.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎的差别很容易被忽略。
senses.why: Latin dis- 'apart' plus ferre 'carry' gives the image of carrying two things apart so that a gap shows.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 dis-「分开」加 ferre「搬运」构成画面：把两样东西搬开，缝隙就显出来。

senses.title: The amount left by subtraction
senses.definition: the amount by which one quantity is larger or smaller than another
senses.definitionCN: 一个量比另一个量多出或少掉的数额
senses.example: The difference between income and outgoings is four hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 收入与支出之间的差额是四百英镑。
senses.why: The gap seen between two amounts is measured by subtracting one from the other.
senses.whyCN: 两个数目之间看到的缝隙，用一数减另一数即可量出。

senses.title: A disagreement
senses.definition: a disagreement of opinion between people or groups
senses.definitionCN: 人或群体之间意见不一致
senses.example: A serious difference over funding split the committee.
senses.exampleCN: 在经费问题上的严重分歧使委员会分裂。
senses.why: Two positions carried apart leave a gap, and that gap in talk is a disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 两个立场被搬开就留下缝隙，话语里的这道缝隙就是分歧。

senses.title: An effect that matters
senses.definition: an effect that changes an outcome in a way that matters
senses.definitionCN: 足以改变结果的效应
senses.example: One extra hour of sleep made a real difference.
senses.exampleCN: 多睡一小时真的带来了改变。
senses.why: The phrase asks whether the gap between two states is wide enough to count.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法问的是：两种状态之间的缝隙是否大到值得计数。

senses.title: A distinguishing feature
senses.definition: a feature by which one kind of thing can be told from another
senses.definitionCN: 用来把一类事物与另一类分开的特征
senses.example: The difference lies in how the two metals are cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 区别在于这两种金属的冷却方式。
senses.why: The feature is the very thing that opens the gap, so English calls the feature a difference too.
senses.whyCN: 那个特征正是打开缝隙的东西，于是英语也把特征本身叫作差别。

senses.title: A mark of individuality
senses.definition: a quality that makes one person or thing distinct
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物显得独特的品质
senses.example: Her voice has a difference that makes it easy to recognise.
senses.exampleCN: 她的嗓音有种一听就能认出的特质。
senses.why: From 'what separates' to 'what distinguishes' is a short step: the gap becomes a signature.
senses.whyCN: 从「分隔之处」到「区别之处」只差一步：缝隙变成了签名。

senses.title: The set-theoretic difference
senses.definition: the set of members belonging to one set but not another
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个集合而不属于另一个集合的那些元素
senses.example: The difference of the two sets contains only the elements unique to the first.
senses.exampleCN: 两个集合的差只含第一个集合独有的元素。
senses.why: Set theory keeps the plain sense: carry the second set away from the first and see what is left.
senses.whyCN: 集合论保留朴素的字面义：把第二个集合从第一个搬走，看看剩下什么。

senses.title: A felt distance between people
senses.titleCN: 抽象：人与人之间可感的距离
senses.definition: a distance between people or things that can be felt rather than measured
senses.definitionCN: 人与人、物与物之间可以感受而非量出的距离
senses.example: Years of silence had opened a difference no letter could close.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的沉默拉开了一道任何信件都补不上的距离。
senses.why: The abstract sense removes measurement: what remains is pure separation, felt as distance.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉度量，只剩纯粹的分离，被感受为距离。

intro.en: Difference comes through Old French from Latin differentia, a noun from differre 'to carry apart, differ', built on dis- 'apart' and ferre 'to carry'.
intro.cn: difference 经古法语来自拉丁 differentia，出自动词 differre「分开搬、相异」，由 dis-「分开」与 ferre「搬运」构成。

items.en: Ferre 'to carry, bear' is an irregular verb; its root is generally traced to an old verb of bearing, a form reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: ferre 意为「搬运、承载」，是不规则动词；其词根一般上溯到一个古老的「承载」动词，此形式属重构而非实证。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus ferre gave differre 'to carry apart, to be unlike'. The prefix does the separating, the root does the moving.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 ferre 构成 differre「分开搬、不同」。前缀负责分开，词根负责搬动。

items.en: The abstract noun differentia named the state of being carried apart, hence a distinction or a gap.
items.cn: 抽象名词 differentia 指被分开的状态，因此指区别或缝隙。

items.en: Old French difference passed into English in the fourteenth century, first as a general term for unlikeness.
items.cn: 古法语 difference 在十四世纪进入英语，最初泛指「不一样」。

items.en: The arithmetic sense of a remainder and the sense of a quarrel both appear in the medieval and early modern record.
items.cn: 算术上的剩余义与争吵义都出现在中世纪及近代早期的书证中。

items.en: The idiom about making a difference is a twentieth-century development, and its first date is only approximate.
items.cn: 「起作用」的这个习语是二十世纪的发展，确切首见年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin carrying root, where only the prefix changes; group two holds nouns for an unlikeness or a gap.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「搬运」词根、只换前缀的词；第二组是表示「不一样」或「间隔」的名词。

entries.definition: The verb from which the noun is formed: to be unlike, or to disagree.
entries.definitionCN: 名词由这个动词构成：不相同，或意见不一。

entries.definition: The adjective describing two things carried apart.
entries.definitionCN: 描述两物被分开的形容词。

entries.definition: From de- plus ferre: a carrying down or yielding, hence respectful submission; it looks like difference but is not.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de- 加 ferre 构成，意为「向下搬、让与」，引申为恭敬顺从；形似而义异。

entries.definition: From the same root, used for a difference in rates or a small change in calculus.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该词根，用于比率之差或微积分中的微小改变。

entries.definition: A difference consciously marked, often one that matters for classification.
entries.definitionCN: 被有意标出的差别，常指对分类有意义的差别。

entries.definition: A large and often unfair difference, used of incomes, conditions and resources.
entries.definitionCN: 大而不常公平的差距，多用于收入、条件与资源。

entries.definition: The empty space between two things, literal or figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 两物之间的空处，可实可虚。

entries.definition: A difference between two things that ought to match, such as figures or stories.
entries.definitionCN: 本应一致的两者之间的不符，如数字或说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The prefix means 'apart' and the root means 'carry': carrying two things apart leaves exactly the gap we call a difference.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「分开」，词根意为「搬」：把两样东西搬开，留下的缝隙就是差别。

normal.en: One family runs differ, different, differently, difference, differentiate and differentiation.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：相异、不同的、不同地、差别、区分、分化。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the main uses: make a difference, tell the difference, settle differences.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出主要用法：起作用、分辨差别、解决分歧。

normal.en: The arithmetic sense is literal: subtract the smaller amount and the gap is the difference.
normal.cn: 算术义最字面：用较小的量减一减，缝隙就是差额。

normal.en: Words from the same root but other prefixes carry in other directions: down in deference, across in differential.
normal.cn: 同根而前缀不同的词把「搬」指向别处：向下是顺从，横向是差分。

abstract.en: Picture two ropes hanging side by side, with one knot placed a hand's width higher than the other.
abstract.cn: 想象两条并排垂下的绳子，一个绳结比另一个高出一掌宽。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking away from each other until the space between them can no longer be crossed by a word.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人越走越远，直到一句话再也跨不过中间的距离。

abstract.en: Picture two almost identical keys, where the only gap is a single notch.
abstract.cn: 想象两把几乎相同的钥匙，唯一的差别只有一道小齿。

examples.en: There is a clear difference between the two samples.
examples.cn: 这两个样本之间有明显的差别。

examples.en: The difference in price is only a few pounds.
examples.cn: 价格上的差额只有几英镑。

examples.en: They settled their differences before the meeting resumed.
examples.cn: 他们在会议继续之前解决了分歧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前缀意为「分开」，词根意为「搬」：把两样东西搬开，中间露出的那道缝就是差别；在数字上量出这道缝，就是差额。

root: 拉丁 differentia「区别」＝ dis-（分开）＋ ferre「搬运」，动词 differre 意为「分开搬、相异」；ferre 的更早词根一般上溯为重构形式。英语经古法语传入；deference 虽形近，却由 de- 加同一词根构成，义为「向下让与」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: two things are carried apart and a gap shows between them. That gap is then measured as a remainder, heard as a quarrel, felt as a distance, and finally seen as the very mark that makes a thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一幅画面展开：把两样东西搬开，中间露出缝隙。这道缝再依次被量成差额、听成分歧、感成距离，最后看成使一物成为它自己的那个标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two lines running side by side with a visible gap between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排延伸的线，中间留着看得见的缝。

branches.en: THE GAP: the unlike respect and the feature that makes it visible are the same seam.
branches.cn: 缝隙：不一样的方面与使它可见的特征，是同一条缝。

branches.en: MEASURE IT: arithmetic and set theory both take one thing away and name what is left.
branches.cn: 量它：算术与集合论都拿走一个，再命名剩下的。

branches.en: QUARREL: two positions held apart leave a gap in talk.
branches.cn: 分歧：两个立场被搬开，话语里就留下缝隙。

branches.en: IT COUNTS: a difference wide enough to matter becomes an effect or a signature.
branches.cn: 算数：宽到足以起作用的差别，会变成一种效应或一个签名。

branches.en: DISTANCE: with no ruler, the gap is simply felt as separation.
branches.cn: 距离：没有尺子时，缝隙就被直接感成分离。

intro.en: Difference is a Latin abstract noun; the prefix separates, the root carries, and the ending turns the act into a state.
intro.cn: difference 是一个拉丁抽象名词；前缀负责分开，词根负责搬运，词尾把动作变成状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre gives differre and differentia; dis- marks separation, and the English ending -ence names a state.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ferre 衍生 differre 与 differentia；dis- 标出分离，英语词尾 -ence 表示状态。

items.example: The prefix does the separating.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀负责分开。

items.example: The root does the moving.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根负责搬动。

items.example: The Latin verb joins separation to carrying.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词把分离与搬运结合起来。

items.example: The noun names the state of being apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被分开的状态。

items.example: The difference is small.
items.exampleCN: 差别很小。

items.example: The two accounts differ in one detail.
items.exampleCN: 两种说法在一个细节上不同。

items.example: They chose a different route.
items.exampleCN: 他们选了另一条路线。

items.meaning: to make distinct; to find a derivative
items.example: Colour helps us differentiate the layers.
items.exampleCN: 颜色帮我们区分这些层次。

definition_zh: 意思是；意味着；打算；平均值；中间值；刻薄的；吝啬的
definition_en: to intend or signify something; also the middle value of a set of numbers, or unkind and unwilling to spend
core_image: 一句含混的话被手指向它真正要说的那件事，旁边天平恰好停在正中
scene: 统计员把五个读数的总和除开，求出中间的那个数值。The mean of the five readings is nine.
sceneCN: 这里指「一组数的平均值」（第 4 个义项：平均数）；句意为五个读数的平均值是九。可辨识物件：记录纸、五个读数、计算器、天平。

senses.title: To have a sense
senses.definition: to have as a meaning, said of a word, sign or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、符号或手势所具有的意思
senses.example: What does this symbol mean?
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号表示什么？
senses.why: The Old English verb mænan meant 'to intend, signify', and a word's sense is what it intends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 mænan 意为「意图、意指」，而词的意思就是它所意图的东西。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to be a sign or indication of something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的迹象或征兆
senses.example: A red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的红霞意味着明天天气晴好。
senses.why: A sign points to what it intends, so the verb extends from words to natural signs.
senses.whyCN: 符号指向它所意指之物，于是这个动词从词语扩展到自然征兆。

senses.title: To intend to do
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事放在心里作为目的
senses.example: I mean to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我打算今晚把报告写完。
senses.why: Intention is the inward side of meaning: what a person means is what he intends.
senses.whyCN: 意图是「意思」的内面：一个人意指什么，就是他打算什么。

senses.title: The average of a set
senses.definition: the value obtained by adding all the numbers and dividing by how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把全部数值相加再除以个数所得的值
senses.example: Add the values and divide by five to get the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些值相加再除以五，就得到平均值。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source: Old French meien 'middle', from Latin medianus, not from the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自另一来源：古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus，与英语动词无关。

senses.title: The middle between extremes
senses.definition: a middle point equally distant from two extremes
senses.definitionCN: 与两个极端等距的中间点
senses.example: The golden mean lies between excess and defect.
senses.exampleCN: 中庸之道位于过度与不足之间。
senses.why: The same 'middle' sense serves ethics as well as arithmetic, naming the point that is neither too much nor too little.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「中间」义既用于算术也用于伦理，指既不过多也不过少的那一点。

senses.title: Unkind in manner
senses.definition: unkind, spiteful or deliberately hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 不友善、带恶意或故意伤人的
senses.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘲笑她的错误，未免刻薄。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a third source, Old English gemæne 'common, shared', whose sense sank from 'common' to 'inferior' and then to 'petty'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自第三个来源，古英语 gemæne「共同的、共享的」，词义从「共同」降到「低劣」，再降到「小气」。

senses.title: Stingy with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or share what one has
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或不愿分享所有
senses.example: He is too mean to buy a second chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他太吝啬，连第二把椅子都不肯买。
senses.why: A person who keeps everything for himself is 'common' in the old sense of ordinary and small, and the word settled into stinginess.
senses.whyCN: 把一切都留给自己的人在旧义上显得「普通而小气」，于是这个词固定为吝啬。

senses.title: Remarkable in the phrase 'no mean'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中意为「不小的」
senses.definition: not small or easy, used in the fixed phrase no mean feat
senses.definitionCN: 不小、不容易，用于固定说法「不小的成就」
senses.example: Finishing the climb in one day was no mean feat.
senses.exampleCN: 一天之内爬完这段路可不是小事。
senses.why: The phrase works by understatement: it denies the small reading of the adjective in order to praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法用反语：否定形容词「小」的那一面，从而达到称赞。

intro.en: Mean has three separate sources that happen to share one spelling: the verb 'to intend' from Old English mænan, the noun 'average' from Old French meien and Latin medianus, and the adjective 'petty, stingy' from Old English gemæne 'common'.
intro.cn: mean 有三个恰好同形的来源：表示「意图」的动词出自古英语 mænan；表示「平均值」的名词出自古法语 meien 与拉丁 medianus；表示「小气、刻薄」的形容词出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」。

items.en: Mænan meant 'to intend, signify'. Its deeper Germanic origin is not settled; the usual comparison with German meinen is a family resemblance rather than a proved derivation.
items.cn: mænan 意为「意图、意指」。其更早的日耳曼来源无定论；通常把它与德语 meinen 相比，那只是同族相似，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Gemæne meant 'common, shared'. The sense passed from 'common' to 'ordinary, inferior' and then to 'petty, stingy', a downward slide recorded in Middle English.
items.cn: gemæne 意为「共同的、共享的」。词义从「共同」经「普通、低劣」滑向「小气、吝啬」，这一下移在中古英语中已有记录。

items.en: Meien 'middle' entered English in the fourteenth century as the name of the middle value, and it is the source of the average sense.
items.cn: meien「中间」在十四世纪进入英语，指居中的那个数值，是平均值义的来源。

items.en: Medianus 'of the middle' comes from medius 'middle', the same root that gives median, medium and mediate.
items.cn: medianus「中间的」出自 medius「中间」，同一词根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.en: English spelling merged the three histories into one written form, which is why a single entry must keep verb, average and adjective apart.
items.cn: 英语拼写把这三段历史并成一个书写形式，因此同一个词条必须把动词、平均值与形容词分开。

items.en: Exact first citations for each strand are approximate: the verb is Old English, the average noun is fourteenth-century, and the stingy adjective is later Middle English.
items.cn: 三条线索的确切首见书证都只是约数：动词属古英语，平均值名词属十四世纪，吝啬形容词属中古英语后期。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives that are easily mistaken for the same word; group two holds words that share one of the three meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被当成同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是分别与三种含义之一相近的词。

entries.definition: The third-person singular of the verb, and separately a plural noun meaning 'resources'; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数，另有一个表示「资源、手段」的复数名词；都不是那个形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb; the spelling no longer shows the vowel of the base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词；拼写已看不出原形元音。

entries.definition: From the same Latin root as the average sense, but it names the middle item of an ordered set, not the sum divided by the count.
entries.definitionCN: 与平均值义同出拉丁词根，但指按序排列后居中的那一项，而非总和除以个数。

entries.definition: Latin medius as a noun: the middle, or a means between two sides; it has nothing to do with intending.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 medius 的名词形式：中间，或两端之间的媒介；与「意图」无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the sum divided by the count; mean is its technical doublet in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指总和除以个数；在统计中 mean 是它的技术性同义词。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something, close to the 'be a sign' sense of mean.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事的符号，接近 mean 的「预示」义。

entries.definition: To have a purpose, the plain equivalent of the 'plan' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有目的，是「打算」义的直白对应词。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend or share, the direct synonym of the adjective in its money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或分享，是形容词在钱财义上的直接同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three histories share one spelling: intend, middle, and common-turned-petty.
normal.cn: 三段历史共用一种拼写：意图、中间、由「共同」转来的小气。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in sound but regular in pattern: means, meant, meant, meaning.
normal.cn: 动词读音不规则但形式规律：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 means、meant、meant、meaning。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: mean to do, mean well, the mean value, no mean feat.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：打算做、出于好意、平均值、不小的成就。

normal.en: The average sense came through French, so it belongs with median and medium rather than with the verb.
normal.cn: 平均值义经法语而来，因此它与 median、medium 同族，而不属于动词那一支。

normal.en: The unkind sense began as 'common', which then meant 'ordinary' and finally 'petty'.
normal.cn: 刻薄义起于「共同的」，再变成「普通的」，最后成了「小气的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at the one thing a vague sentence was trying to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指出一句含混的话真正想说的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales settling exactly level, with equal weights on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平恰好停在水平位置，两边重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a man counting coins twice before he will spend a single one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把硬币数了两遍才肯花掉一枚。

examples.en: A green light means that the road is clear.
examples.cn: 绿灯表示道路畅通。

examples.en: The mean of the class scores rose after the extra lesson.
examples.cn: 加课之后，全班成绩的平均值上升了。

examples.en: It was mean of them to leave her out of the invitation.
examples.cn: 他们把她排除在邀请之外，实在刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词那一支表示「意图、意指」；平均值那一支来自法语里的「中间」；形容词那一支从「共同的」滑到「普通」，再滑到「小气」。三支同形，要按上下文分开。

root: 三条互不同源的线索合成一个拼写：动词出自古英语 mænan「意图、意指」，更早来源无定论；平均值义出自古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus、medius；形容词义出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」，词义下滑为「低劣、小气」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses come from three histories: intending and signifying, the middle value, and the small or petty. The entry keeps them apart so that no sentence is read through the wrong history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项来自三段历史：意图与意指、居中的数值、以及小气刻薄。本词条把它们分开，免得用错历史去读一个句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at what a sentence intends, while a balance beside it rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一句话所意图的东西，旁边的天平恰好水平。

branches.en: SIGNIFY: a word and a red sky both point to what they intend.
branches.cn: 意指：一个词与一片红霞都指向它们所意图的东西。

branches.en: INTEND: purpose is what a person means to do.
branches.cn: 意图：目的就是一个人打算做的事。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE: the average and the golden mean are one position seen numerically and ethically.
branches.cn: 中间：平均值与中庸是同一点在数字与伦理上的两个看法。

branches.en: COMMON TO PETTY: the adjective slid from shared to ordinary to stingy.
branches.cn: 由共同到小气：形容词从「共享」滑到「普通」再到「吝啬」。

branches.en: UNDERSTATEMENT: denying 'small' is a way of saying 'large'.
branches.cn: 反语：否定「小」，正是说「大」。

intro.en: One spelling serves three families, so the affix view must be split: a Germanic verb, a Germanic adjective, and a Latin root for the middle.
intro.cn: 一种拼写服务于三个词族，因此按语素读时必须拆开：一个日耳曼动词、一个日耳曼形容词，以及一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The verb family is Germanic, with no Latin kin; the average sense belongs to Latin medius, which also gives median, medium and mediate.
latinIntro.cn: 动词一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族；平均值义属拉丁 medius，同根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.example: The Old English verb is the source of the 'signify' senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是「意指」诸义的来源。

items.example: The adjective began as 'shared' and ended as 'stingy'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「共享」开始，最后落到「吝啬」。

items.example: The Latin root supplies the average and middle senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词根提供平均值与中间诸义。

items.example: The derived adjective gives median.
items.exampleCN: 这个派生形容词给出 median。

items.example: I mean the second door.
items.exampleCN: 我指的是第二扇门。

items.structure: mean + -ing (noun suffix, result of an action)
items.example: The meaning is clear.
items.exampleCN: 意思很清楚。

items.meaning: in a petty or stingy way
items.example: He spoke meanly of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 他刻薄地评价那个提议。

items.meaning: the quality of being petty or stingy
items.example: Their meanness surprised the guests.
items.exampleCN: 他们的吝啬让客人吃惊。

latinEntries.structure: medius, media, medium (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 中位数；中线；中间值；中央分隔带；正中的
definition_en: the middle value of a set of numbers arranged in order, or a line or strip running through the middle
core_image: 一排高低不齐的柱子按高度站好，正中间那一根被圈出来
scene: 研究者在把七份薪水从低到高排好后，圈出了正中间的那一份。The median of the seven salaries is lower than the average.
sceneCN: 这里指「按大小排好后位于正中间的那个数」（第 1 个义项：统计中的中位数）；句意为七份薪水的中位数低于平均值。可辨识物件：薪水单、排序标尺、红圈、直尺。

pos.zh: 中位数；中线；中间值；中央分隔带

senses.title: The middle value in statistics
senses.definition: the value that divides an ordered set into two equal halves
senses.definitionCN: 把一个按序排列的集合分成相等两半的那个值
senses.example: The median of the seven salaries is lower than the average.
senses.exampleCN: 七份薪水的中位数低于平均值。
senses.why: Medianus means 'of the middle', and statistics simply names the item that stands at the middle of an ordered row.
senses.whyCN: medianus 意为「中间的」，统计学只是把按序排好后站在中间的那一项命名为中位数。

senses.title: A line from a vertex to the midpoint
senses.definition: a line drawn from a vertex of a triangle to the midpoint of the opposite side
senses.definitionCN: 从三角形一个顶点画到对边中点的线段
senses.example: The three medians of a triangle meet at a single point.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形的三条中线交于一点。
senses.why: The geometric line runs to the middle of the opposite side, so the same word serves geometry.
senses.whyCN: 这条几何线通向对边的中点，因此同一个词也用于几何。

senses.title: A middle point in general
senses.definition: a point or value lying in the middle of a range
senses.definitionCN: 落在某个范围中间的点或值
senses.example: The median of the range falls halfway between the two extremes.
senses.exampleCN: 这一范围的中间值落在两个极端之间。
senses.why: The general sense is the plain reading of the Latin adjective, before any technical use.
senses.whyCN: 一般义是那个拉丁形容词最朴素的读法，早于任何技术用法。

senses.title: A strip dividing a road
senses.definition: the strip of ground that separates opposing lanes of traffic
senses.definitionCN: 把相反方向车道隔开的那条地带
senses.example: A low hedge runs along the median for two miles.
senses.exampleCN: 一条低矮的树篱沿着中央分隔带延伸两英里。
senses.why: The strip occupies the middle of the road, so the middle-value word was borrowed for it.
senses.whyCN: 这条地带占着道路的中间，于是表示「中间」的词被借来指它。

senses.title: A structure at the body's midline
senses.definition: an anatomical structure lying along the midline of the body
senses.definitionCN: 沿人体正中线分布的解剖结构
senses.example: The median nerve passes through the wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 正中神经经过腕部。
senses.why: Anatomy uses the adjective for anything placed on the midline, keeping the literal spatial sense.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把这个形容词用于一切位于正中线上的结构，保留了字面的空间义。

senses.title: Middle in position or value
senses.definition: occupying or representing the middle of a range
senses.definitionCN: 占据或代表某个范围的中间
senses.example: The median age of the group is thirty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 这个群体的年龄中位数是三十二岁。
senses.why: As an adjective the word simply places something in the middle, whether in space or in a ranked list.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，这个词只是把某物放在中间，无论指空间还是指排序。

senses.title: The midline of a trapezoid
senses.definition: the segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides of a trapezoid
senses.definitionCN: 连接梯形两条非平行边中点的线段
senses.example: Its length equals the average of the two parallel sides.
senses.exampleCN: 它的长度等于两条平行边的平均值。
senses.why: The segment sits halfway between the parallel sides, so geometry calls it a median as well.
senses.whyCN: 这条线段位于两条平行边之间的正中，几何学同样称它为中位线。

senses.title: The median voter in politics
senses.definition: the voter at the middle of the distribution of opinions
senses.definitionCN: 意见分布中处于中间位置的那位选民
senses.example: A candidate must win the median voter to take the seat.
senses.exampleCN: 候选人必须赢得中位选民才能拿下这个席位。
senses.why: Political science applies the statistical middle to opinions: whoever stands at the centre of the distribution decides the contest.
senses.whyCN: 政治学把统计上的中间用到意见上：站在分布中心的人决定胜负。

intro.en: Median comes from Latin medianus 'of the middle', an adjective from medius 'middle'; English took it directly from Latin in the sixteenth century, probably with French mediation.
intro.cn: median 出自拉丁形容词 medianus「中间的」，其词根为 medius「中间」；英语在十六世纪直接取自拉丁语，可能经法语中转。

items.en: Medius meant 'middle, in the middle'. It is generally traced to an old root for 'middle', a reconstructed form rather than a written record.
items.cn: medius 意为「中间的、在中间」。它一般被上溯到一个表示「中间」的古老词根，此形式属重构而非书面记录。

items.en: Medius plus the adjective ending -anus produced medianus 'of the middle, middlemost'.
items.cn: medius 加形容词词尾 -anus 构成 medianus「中间的、最当中的」。

items.en: The form passed through Late Latin and French usage before entering English, where it first described things lying in the middle.
items.cn: 这一形式经晚期拉丁语与法语用法，再进入英语，最初描述位于中间的事物。

items.en: The geometric sense of a line to the midpoint is old in Latin mathematical writing and passed into English with the word.
items.cn: 「通到中点的线」这一几何义在拉丁数学文献中已很古老，随词一同进入英语。

items.en: The statistical sense of the middle value is a nineteenth-century development, fixed as ordinary technical vocabulary in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「居中数值」的统计义是十九世纪的发展，到二十世纪固定为常用技术词汇。

items.en: The road strip and the anatomical uses are later transfers of the plain spatial sense; their exact first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 道路分隔带与解剖学用法都是空间义的较晚转移，确切首见年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin middle root, where prefix or ending is all that differs; group two holds words for a central value or position.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「中间」词根、只差前缀或词尾的词；第二组是表示中心值或中心位置的词。

entries.definition: The Latin neuter form used as a noun: something in the middle, hence a means or a material.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁中性形式作名词用：居中之物，引申为手段或媒材。

entries.definition: To stand in the middle between two parties; the verb keeps the spatial picture.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方中间，动词保留了空间画面。

entries.definition: In- 'not' plus mediatus 'middle': with nothing in between, hence direct.
entries.definitionCN: in-「不」加 mediatus「中间」：中间没有东西，故指直接。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus medius: lying between two stages or levels.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「在……之间」加 medius：位于两个阶段或层次之间。

entries.definition: A calculated value, which may differ from the middle item when the data are skewed.
entries.definitionCN: 由总和除以个数算出的值，数据偏斜时可能与居中那一项不同。

entries.definition: The point equally distant from both ends of a line or range.
entries.definitionCN: 与线段或范围两端等距的点。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the central part, with no technical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 表示中央部分的日常词，不含技术义。

entries.definition: The middle of a space or an activity, often a point of concentration.
entries.definitionCN: 空间或活动的中心，常指聚集之点。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'middle', so every sense puts something at the centre of a row, a road, a body or a triangle.
normal.cn: 词根意为「中间」，因此每个义项都是把某物放在一列数、一条路、一个人体或一个三角形的中央。

normal.en: One family runs median, medial, medium, mediate and intermediate.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：中位数、内侧的、媒介、调解、中间的。

normal.en: The negated relative is immediate: nothing in the middle means direct.
normal.cn: 加了否定前缀的亲属词是 immediate：中间没有东西，就是直接。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: median income, median age, the median strip, the median voter.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：收入中位数、年龄中位数、中央分隔带、中位选民。

normal.en: In a triangle the three medians meet at one point, so the word always points to the halfway mark.
normal.cn: 在三角形里三条中线交于一点，可见这个词总指向「一半处」的标记。

abstract.en: Picture a row of pillars of different heights with the middle one marked by a ring of paint.
abstract.cn: 想象一排高低不同的柱子，正中间那根被画上一圈颜料。

abstract.en: Picture a road divided by a narrow green strip, with traffic flowing on either side.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被窄窄的绿带分开的道路，两侧车流各自前行。

abstract.en: Picture a line drawn from the tip of a triangle straight to the middle of the wall opposite.
abstract.cn: 想象从三角形顶点笔直画到对面墙正中的一条线。

examples.en: The median divides the ordered list into two equal halves.
examples.cn: 中位数把排好序的列表分成相等的两半。

examples.en: Median income in the region has barely moved.
examples.cn: 该地区的收入中位数几乎没有变化。

examples.en: The median strip was planted with low shrubs.
examples.cn: 中央分隔带上种了低矮的灌木。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「中间」，加形容词词尾表示「属于中间的」：把一列数按大小排好，站在正中的那一项就是中位数；一条路正中的地带就是中央分隔带。

root: 拉丁 medianus「中间的」＝ medius「中间」＋形容词词尾 -anus；medius 更早词根属重构形式。英语十六世纪直接取自拉丁语，可能经法语中转。同根词 medium、mediate、immediate、intermediate 只差前缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all place one thing at the centre: a value in a ranked list, a line to the midpoint, a strip in a road, a nerve on the body's midline, and a voter at the middle of opinion. The word never leaves the halfway mark.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某物放在正中：排序列表里的一个值、通向中点的一条线、道路正中的一条带、身体正中线上的一条神经，以及意见分布正中的一位选民。这个词始终不离「一半处」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of columns ordered by height, with the middle one circled.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按高度排好的柱子，正中间那根被圈出。

branches.en: MIDDLE VALUE: statistics and ordinary speech both name what stands halfway.
branches.cn: 中间值：统计学与日常说法都指站在一半处的那个。

branches.en: MIDPOINT: geometry draws to the middle of the opposite side.
branches.cn: 中点：几何把线画到对边的正中。

branches.en: THE ROAD: a strip occupies the middle of the carriageway.
branches.cn: 道路：一条地带占据车道的正中。

branches.en: POSITION: anatomy and ordinary adjectives place a structure on the midline.
branches.cn: 位置：解剖学与普通形容词都把结构放在正中线上。

branches.en: OPINION: politics applies the statistical middle to a distribution of views.
branches.cn: 意见：政治学把统计上的中间用到意见分布上。

intro.en: Median is a Latin adjective in English dress; the root medius also builds the nouns and verbs for means and mediation.
intro.cn: median 是一个穿上英语外衣的拉丁形容词；词根 medius 还构成表示手段与调解的名词和动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin medius yields medianus, medietas, medium and mediare; in- and inter- reverse or relocate the middle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 medius 衍生 medianus、medietas、medium、mediare；前缀 in- 与 inter- 否定或移动「中间」。

items.example: The root places something at the centre.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把某物放到中央。

items.example: The suffix turns the root into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把词根变成形容词。

items.example: The Latin adjective is the direct source of median.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁形容词是 median 的直接来源。

items.meaning: the middle value; middle in position
items.example: The median income rose.
items.exampleCN: 收入中位数上升了。

items.example: The medial nerve runs along the arm.
items.exampleCN: 内侧神经沿手臂分布。

items.structure: medius, neuter form used as a noun
items.example: Water is the medium for the reaction.
items.exampleCN: 水是这个反应的介质。

items.example: A neutral party mediated the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 一个中立方调解了这场争端。

items.example: An intermediate layer separates the two.
items.exampleCN: 一个中间层把两者隔开。

definition_zh: 方差；差异；不一致；变动；变通许可
definition_en: the state of differing or changing, or the statistical measure of how far values spread from their mean
core_image: 一排刻度各自偏离中心线，偏离越远越散，幅度越大
scene: 审计员比对两套账目，发现同一笔支出被记成了两个不同的数。The two auditors could not explain the variance between the accounts.
sceneCN: 这里指「两套记录之间的不一致」（第 3 个义项：不一致、不符）；句意为两位审计员无法解释两套账目之间的不符。可辨识物件：账本、两列数字、红笔、计算器。

pos.zh: 方差；差异；不一致；变动；变通许可

senses.title: The statistical measure of spread
senses.definition: the average of the squared distances of values from their mean
senses.definitionCN: 各个数值与平均值之差的平方的平均值
senses.example: A large variance means the readings are widely scattered.
senses.exampleCN: 方差大说明各读数分散得很开。
senses.why: The word names the state of differing, and statistics turns that state into one number.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名「不一样」的状态，统计学把这种状态化成一个数。

senses.title: A difference in amount or level
senses.definition: a difference between two amounts, levels or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 两个数量、水平或状况之间的不同
senses.example: A small variance in temperature is normal in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 春天温度有些小波动是正常的。
senses.why: The noun is built on the verb 'to vary', so any departure from a standard is a variance.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词由「变化」动词构成，凡偏离标准的都算一种差异。

senses.title: A failure to agree
senses.definition: a disagreement between two records, accounts or statements
senses.definitionCN: 两份记录、账目或说法之间的不符
senses.example: The auditors could not explain the variance between the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计员无法解释两套账目之间的不符。
senses.why: Two records that vary from each other leave a discrepancy, and the noun covers that gap too.
senses.whyCN: 两份互不相同的记录留下不符，这个名词也覆盖那道缝。

senses.title: Change from one state to another
senses.definition: the fact of changing or fluctuating over time
senses.definitionCN: 随时间变化或起伏的事实
senses.example: Variances in demand make staffing difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 需求的波动使排班变得困难。
senses.why: Varying is an activity, and the noun names its occurrence, especially when it repeats.
senses.whyCN: 「变化」是一个活动，名词命名它的发生，尤其指反复发生。

senses.title: Permission to depart from a rule
senses.definition: official permission to differ from a zoning or building rule
senses.definitionCN: 获准不遵守某条规划或建筑规则的正式许可
senses.example: The owner applied for a variance to build closer to the road.
senses.exampleCN: 业主申请变通许可，以便把房子建得离路更近。
senses.why: Law borrows the word because the applicant asks to vary from the rule without breaking it.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用这个词，因为申请人请求在不违规的前提下偏离规则。

senses.title: The gap between budget and actual
senses.titleCN: 预算与实际之间的差异
senses.definition: the difference between a planned figure and the figure actually recorded
senses.definitionCN: 计划数字与实际记录数字之间的差
senses.example: A favourable budget variance appeared in the third quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第三季度出现了有利的预算差异。
senses.why: Accounting gives every departure from plan a line, and calls that line a variance.
senses.whyCN: 会计给每一处偏离计划的地方列一行，并称这一行为差异。

senses.title: The sample variance
senses.definition: the statistic computed from a sample, usually with a divisor one less than the count
senses.definitionCN: 由样本算出的统计量，除数通常比个数少一
senses.example: The sample variance slightly overstates the spread of small samples.
senses.exampleCN: 样本方差会略微高估小样本的离散程度。
senses.why: Sample and population versions differ only in the divisor, so one word covers both with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 样本与总体两个版本只差除数，因此一个词加个限定语就能覆盖两者。

senses.title: The degree of departure from the norm
senses.definition: the extent to which something departs from what is usual or expected
senses.definitionCN: 某事物偏离通常或预期状态的程度
senses.example: Any variance from the usual pattern was noted in the log.
senses.exampleCN: 凡偏离常规模式之处都记进了日志。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps only the idea of departure, with no numbers and no rule attached.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留「偏离」这个观念，既不附数字，也不附规则。

intro.en: Variance comes through Old French from Latin variantia, a noun from variare 'to change', itself from varius 'diverse, mottled'. The origin of varius is not fully settled.
intro.cn: variance 经古法语来自拉丁 variantia，出自动词 variare「变化」，再上溯形容词 varius「多样的、斑驳的」；varius 的更早来源尚无定论。

items.en: Varius meant 'diverse, varied, mottled'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; connections proposed to other roots are hypotheses, not demonstrated links.
items.cn: varius 意为「多样的、变化的、斑驳的」。其更早来源不确定；与别的词根的联系只是假说，未获证明。

items.en: Variare 'to change, vary' turned the adjective into a verb of altering.
items.cn: variare「改变、使变化」把形容词变成表示改变的动作词。

items.en: Variantia named the state of being varied, hence a difference or a divergence.
items.cn: variantia 指「有变化」的状态，因此指差异或背离。

items.en: Old French variance carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first as the state of disagreeing.
items.cn: 古法语 variance 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指意见不合的状态。

items.en: The technical sense of squared spread belongs to nineteenth-century statistics and was standardised in the twentieth.
