items.cn: 「平方离散」的技术义属十九世纪统计学，到二十世纪才标准化。

items.en: The permission sense and the budget sense are specialised offshoots; neither has a firmly dated first citation.
items.cn: 许可义与预算义都是专门化的分支，两者的确切首见书证都无定论。

note.en: Group one holds formations from the same varying root that are constantly swapped; group two holds words for a departure or a disagreement.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「变化」词根、常被混用的构词；第二组是表示「偏离」或「不一致」的词。

entries.definition: A single differing form or version, not the state of differing.
entries.definitionCN: 一个具体的不同形式或版本，而非「不一样」的状态。

entries.definition: The process or extent of change, often deliberate or gradual.
entries.definitionCN: 变化的过程或幅度，常指有意的或渐进的改变。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning several different kinds, with no measurement implied.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，指若干不同种类，不含度量之意。

entries.definition: The quality of having many different kinds, used of goods, species or experience.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有许多不同种类的性质，用于商品、物种或体验。

entries.definition: A departure from a standard or a course, usually measured against a norm.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离标准或航道的程度，通常对照某个规范来量。

entries.definition: A mismatch between two things that ought to agree, such as accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 本应一致的两者之间的不符，如账目。

entries.definition: Repeated up-and-down movement in a level or price.
entries.definitionCN: 水平或价格的反复升降。

entries.definition: The general word for two things not being the same.
entries.definitionCN: 表示两事物不一样的通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'varied, mottled', so the noun names the state of not being uniform.
normal.cn: 词根意为「多样的、斑驳的」，因此这个名词指「不齐一」的状态。

normal.en: One family runs vary, variant, variation, variable, variability and variance.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：变化、变体、变化、变量、变异性、方差。

normal.en: Statistics uses the squared distances from the mean; the plain word uses any departure at all.
normal.cn: 统计学用与平均值之差的平方；日常用法则指任何偏离。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the specialised uses: at variance with, budget variance, zoning variance.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出专门用法：与某物不一致、预算差异、规划变通许可。

normal.en: Two records that will not agree are 'at variance', which is the same idea as two numbers that scatter.
normal.cn: 两份对不上的记录叫「不一致」，这与两个散开的数字是同一想法。

abstract.en: Picture a row of marks drifting away from a centre line, some far, some near.
abstract.cn: 想象一排记号偏离中心线，有的远，有的近。

abstract.en: Picture two ledger books open side by side with one figure circled in each, and the circles not matching.
abstract.cn: 想象两本账册并排摊开，每本上圈着一个数字，两个圈却对不上。

abstract.en: Picture a road where one house is allowed to stand a little closer to the kerb than the rule says.
abstract.cn: 想象一条路上有一户获准比规定稍微靠近路缘建房。

examples.en: The variance of the sample was larger than expected.
examples.cn: 这个样本的方差比预期大。

examples.en: Her account is at variance with the official record.
examples.cn: 她的说法与官方记录不一致。

examples.en: The council granted a variance for the taller sign.
examples.cn: 议会批准了这块更高招牌的变通许可。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「多样的、斑驳的」，动词意为「变化」，加名词词尾就成「不一样的状态」；统计学把这种散开化成一个数，法律则把偏离规则的特许也叫这个名字。

root: 拉丁 variantia「差异」＝ variare「变化」＋名词词尾，variare 出自动词化之前的形容词 varius「多样的、斑驳的」；varius 更早来源不确定。英语经古法语传入。同族 vary、variant、variation、variable 只差词尾。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one state: things that were expected to be alike are not. That state is then counted as squared spread, seen as a fluctuation, booked as a ledger gap, licensed by law, and finally named as any departure from the norm.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种状态展开：本应一样的东西并不一样。这种状态再依次被算成平方离散、看成波动、记成账目差额、由法律特许，最后被命名为任何偏离常规的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: marks on a rule drifting away from the centre line, some far and some near.
core.cn: 核心意象：尺上的记号一个个偏离中心线，有的远有的近。

branches.en: MEASURE: the statistical sense turns unlikeness into one squared number, with sample and population versions.
branches.cn: 度量：统计义把「不一样」化成一个平方数，并分样本与总体两个版本。

branches.en: DRIFT: a difference in level and a fluctuation over time are the same departure, seen once and seen repeatedly.
branches.cn: 漂移：水平上的差异与时间上的波动，是同一种偏离的一次看法与反复看法。

branches.en: RECORDS: two sets of figures that will not agree, whether in an audit or a budget.
branches.cn: 记录：两套对不上的数字，无论在审计里还是在预算里。

branches.en: LICENCE: law lets an applicant differ from a rule without breaking it.
branches.cn: 特许：法律允许申请人偏离规则而不违规。

branches.en: THE NORM: with numbers gone, variance is simply distance from what is usual.
branches.cn: 常规：数字去掉之后，方差就是与通常状态的距离。

intro.en: Variance is a Latin abstract noun built on a verb of changing, and the whole family turns up in English with different endings.
intro.cn: variance 是一个拉丁抽象名词，建立在表示变化的动词上；整个词族以不同词尾出现在英语中。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius and variare give variance, variant, variation and variable; the ending -antia becomes English -ance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 与 variare 衍生 variance、variant、variation、variable；词尾 -antia 在英语中变为 -ance。

items.example: The adjective supplies the idea of not being uniform.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供「不齐一」的意思。

items.example: The verb turns the quality into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把性质变成动作。

items.example: The noun names the state, not the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指状态，而非动作。

items.example: The variance was recorded.
items.exampleCN: 差异被记录了下来。

items.example: Prices vary by season.
items.exampleCN: 价格随季节变化。

items.example: A new variant appeared.
items.exampleCN: 出现了一个新变体。

items.meaning: the act or result of varying
items.example: Seasonal variation is expected.
items.exampleCN: 季节性变化在意料之中。

items.example: The variable was poorly measured.
items.exampleCN: 这个变量测得不好。

definition_zh: 标准差；样本标准差；总体标准差；离散程度；波动幅度
definition_en: a statistical measure of how widely values spread around their mean, equal to the square root of the variance
core_image: 一条钟形曲线两侧的坡，坡越缓，数据离中心越远
scene: 老师在黑板上画出成绩分布，并标出数据偏离平均值的典型幅度。A small standard deviation means the scores cluster near the average.
sceneCN: 这里指「衡量数据偏离平均值多远的统计量」（第 1 个义项：标准差）；句意为标准差小，说明分数都挤在平均值附近。可辨识物件：黑板、曲线、中心线、刻度。

pos.zh: 标准差；离散程度；波动幅度

senses.title: The statistical measure
senses.definition: the square root of the variance, expressing spread in the original units
senses.definitionCN: 方差的平方根，用原有单位表示离散程度
senses.example: A small standard deviation means the scores cluster near the average.
senses.exampleCN: 标准差小，说明分数都挤在平均值附近。
senses.why: Deviation is a turning off the road, and statistics uses it for distance from the mean; taking the square root returns the measure to ordinary units.
senses.whyCN: 「偏离」本指离开道路，统计学用它指离平均值的距离；开平方使这个量回到普通单位。

senses.title: The sample standard deviation
senses.definition: the estimate computed from a sample, usually with a divisor one less than the count
senses.definitionCN: 由样本算出的估计值，除数通常比个数少一
senses.example: The sample standard deviation was reported with the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 报告把样本标准差与平均值一起列出。
senses.why: A sample is only part of a population, so its version carries a small correction in the divisor.
senses.whyCN: 样本只是总体的一部分，因此它的版本在除数上有一个小修正。

senses.title: The population standard deviation
senses.definition: the measure computed when every member of a population is known
senses.definitionCN: 已知总体每一个成员时算出的量
senses.example: The population standard deviation is often denoted by a single letter.
senses.exampleCN: 总体标准差常用一个希腊字母表示。
senses.why: With the whole population in hand there is nothing to correct, so the divisor is simply the count.
senses.whyCN: 手里有整个总体时无需修正，除数就是个数本身。

senses.title: A way of stating spread
senses.definition: a way of saying how far values typically lie from the centre
senses.definitionCN: 说明数值通常离中心多远的说法
senses.example: The two classes differ by one standard deviation in height.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个班的身高相差一个标准差。
senses.why: The measure is useful because it can be spoken of in units of itself, turning spread into a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个量好用，是因为可以用它自己的单位来说它，从而把离散变成一把尺。

senses.title: A measure of market volatility
senses.titleCN: 金融市场中的波动度量
senses.definition: a quantity used to express how much a price or return tends to move
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示价格或收益通常变动多少的量
senses.example: Traders quote the standard deviation of daily returns.
senses.exampleCN: 交易员报出日收益的标准差。
senses.why: Finance needs a single number for how far returns stray from their average, and the statistical measure supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 金融需要一个数来表示收益偏离平均多少，统计量正好提供。

senses.title: A process-control figure
senses.titleCN: 质量控制中的过程波动
senses.definition: a figure used in industry to describe how much a process varies around its target
senses.definitionCN: 工业上用来描述过程围绕目标值波动多少的量
senses.example: The line was stopped when the standard deviation exceeded the limit.
senses.exampleCN: 标准差超过限值时，生产线被停了下来。
senses.why: Manufacturing compares each batch with a target, and the measure turns that comparison into a control rule.
senses.whyCN: 制造把每批产品与目标比对，这个量把比对变成一条控制规则。

senses.title: A figure in error analysis
senses.titleCN: 误差分析中的离散指标
senses.definition: a quantity describing the scatter of repeated measurements
senses.definitionCN: 描述重复测量结果散布程度的量
senses.example: Repeated readings were reported with their standard deviation.
senses.exampleCN: 重复读数连同其标准差一起报告。
senses.why: Repeated measurements rarely agree exactly, and the measure summarises that disagreement in one number.
senses.whyCN: 重复测量很少完全一致，这个量把这种不一致收进一个数。

senses.title: The typical distance from the average
senses.titleCN: 抽象：偏离平均的典型幅度
senses.definition: a plain way of naming how far a thing usually stands from what is typical
senses.definitionCN: 用朴素说法指出某物通常离通常状态有多远
senses.example: In that family, lateness beyond a standard deviation was rare.
senses.exampleCN: 在那家人里，迟到超过一个典型幅度的情况很少见。
senses.why: The abstract sense drops the arithmetic and keeps the picture: a usual distance from the centre.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义去掉算术，只保留画面：离中心的一段惯常距离。

intro.en: Standard deviation joins two words of different origin. Standard comes from Old French estandart 'rallying banner', from a Germanic compound meaning 'stand firm'; deviation comes from Latin deviare 'to turn off the road'. The statistical term was named in the late nineteenth century.
intro.cn: standard deviation 由两个来源不同的词合成。standard 出自古法语 estandart「集合旗」，再上溯一个意为「站稳」的日耳曼复合词；deviation 出自拉丁 deviare「离开道路」。这个统计术语在十九世纪后期得名。

items.en: The Germanic source meant 'stand firm, stand hard'. The form is reconstructed from the French and Germanic records, so it is a reconstruction rather than an attested word.
items.cn: 其日耳曼来源意为「站稳、立定」。这一形式由法语与日耳曼语的书证重构而来，属重构形式，并非有直接记录的词。

items.en: Estandart named a rallying banner, the fixed point troops gathered around; English standard kept both the banner and the fixed-point senses.
items.cn: estandart 指集合旗，即部队聚集的固定点；英语 standard 同时保留「旗」与「固定点」两义。

items.en: Via meant 'way, road'. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and any older root offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: via 意为「道路」。其更早来源不确定，凡为其拟出的更古老词根都属假说。

items.en: De- 'off' plus via produced deviare 'to leave the road, stray'; deviatio named the straying.
items.cn: de-「离开」加 via 构成 deviare「离开道路、走偏」；deviatio 指这种偏离。

items.en: The phrase standard deviation was introduced in the 1890s in the circle of Karl Pearson to name the square root of the mean squared deviation; the naming is documented, though early uses vary.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪九十年代由皮尔逊一系学者引入，用来命名均方偏差的平方根；命名过程有文献可查，早期用法略有出入。

items.en: From statistics the term spread into finance, manufacturing and measurement, where it now names any typical distance from a target.
items.cn: 这个词从统计学扩散到金融、制造与测量，如今指任何离目标的惯常距离。

note.en: Group one holds technical neighbours whose names are easily confused with standard deviation; group two holds words for spread or departure.
note.cn: 第一组是名称极易与标准差混淆的技术近邻；第二组是表示散布或偏离的词。

entries.definition: The standard deviation of a sample's mean, not of the values themselves; it shrinks as the sample grows.
entries.definitionCN: 指样本平均值的标准差，而非各个数值的标准差；样本越大它越小。

entries.definition: A value expressed in units of standard deviation from the mean, also called a z-score.
entries.definitionCN: 用「离平均值多少个标准差」表示的值，也称 z 分数。

entries.definition: The distance of one value from the mean without squaring and without a square root.
entries.definitionCN: 单个值离平均值的距离，既不开方也不平方。

entries.definition: The average squared deviation; its square root is the standard deviation.
entries.definitionCN: 平方偏差的平均值；它的平方根就是标准差。

entries.definition: Any measure of how widely values are distributed, of which the standard deviation is one.
entries.definitionCN: 衡量数值分布宽窄的任何量，标准差只是其中一种。

entries.definition: The range or width of a distribution in ordinary language.
entries.definitionCN: 日常语言里指一个分布的跨度或宽度。

entries.definition: The difference between the highest and lowest values, a cruder measure of spread.
entries.definitionCN: 最大值与最小值之差，是更粗疏的离散度量。

entries.definition: A departure from a standard or a course, the plain word behind the technical phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 偏离标准或航道，是这个技术短语背后的普通词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The phrase is two words: a fixed standard plus a turning off the road; statistics measures distance from the mean.
normal.cn: 这个短语由两个词组成：固定的标准，加一次离开道路；统计学用它量离平均值的距离。

normal.en: The measure is the square root of the variance, so the two always appear together.
normal.cn: 这个量是方差的平方根，因此两者总是成对出现。

normal.en: Standard error and standard score are neighbours with different jobs: one is about a mean, the other about a converted value.
normal.cn: 标准误与标准分数是职责不同的邻居：一个关于平均值，一个关于换算后的值。

normal.en: The usual shorthand is a pair of letters or a single Greek letter for the population version.
normal.cn: 常用简写是两个字母，或用一个希腊字母表示总体版本。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: sample standard deviation, within one standard deviation, daily returns.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：样本标准差、在一个标准差之内、日收益。

abstract.en: Picture a bell-shaped hill; a steep pair of slopes means everything stays near the top, a gentle pair means it wanders far.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟形的山丘：坡陡说明东西都留在山顶附近，坡缓说明它跑得很远。

abstract.en: Picture a target with shots scattered around the centre, most inside a ring of one width.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靶子，弹着点散在中心周围，多数落在宽度相同的一圈之内。

abstract.en: Picture a factory line where every batch must stay inside a band of fixed width, or the line stops.
abstract.cn: 想象一条生产线，每批产品都必须留在一条固定宽度的带子里，否则就停机。

examples.en: The report gives the mean and the standard deviation for each group.
examples.cn: 报告给出每一组的平均值与标准差。

examples.en: Returns moved by more than one standard deviation on that day.
examples.cn: 那天的收益变动超过了一个标准差。

examples.en: A wide standard deviation warns that the process is unstable.
examples.cn: 标准差偏大，说明这个过程不稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前一个词是「固定的标准」，后一个词是「离开道路」：合起来就是「各个数值通常离平均值多远」的量。它等于方差的平方根，用原有单位说话。

root: 复合术语。standard 出自古法语 estandart「集合旗」，再上溯意为「站稳」的日耳曼复合词，该形式为重构；deviation 出自拉丁 deviare「离开道路」＝ de-（离开）＋ via「道路」，via 更早来源不确定。统计义在十九世纪九十年代命名。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all measure one thing: how far values usually stand from their centre. The same figure is then read as a sample estimate, a population value, a scale for comparison, a market volatility, a control limit, a measurement error and, at last, a plain typical distance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在量同一件事：各个数值通常离它们的中心多远。同一个量再依次读作样本估计、总体值、比较用的尺度、市场波动、控制限、测量误差，最后读作朴素的惯常距离。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bell-shaped hill whose slopes show how far things wander from the top.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座钟形山丘，两侧的坡显示东西离山顶能跑多远。

branches.en: ONE NUMBER: the measure exists in sample and population versions that differ only in the divisor.
branches.cn: 一个数：这个量有样本与总体两个版本，只差除数。

branches.en: A SCALE: spread can be stated in units of itself, which also summarises measurement error.
branches.cn: 一把尺：离散可以用它自己的单位来说，这也顺带概括了测量误差。

branches.en: MARKET SWING: finance borrows the measure for how far returns stray.
branches.cn: 市场摆动：金融借用这个量表示收益偏离多远。

branches.en: CONTROL LIMIT: industry turns the measure into a rule that stops a line.
branches.cn: 控制限：工业把这个量变成一条停机的规则。

branches.en: TYPICAL DISTANCE: with the arithmetic dropped, it is simply how far things usually stand from the centre.
branches.cn: 惯常距离：去掉算术之后，它就是东西通常离中心多远。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Germanic noun and a Latin verb, so its parts come from two different families and should be read separately.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个日耳曼名词与一个拉丁动词构成，两部分来自不同词族，应分开来读。

latinIntro.en: Germanic stand gives standard; Latin via and deviare give deviate and deviation. The two halves meet only in the technical phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 日耳曼语 stand 给出 standard；拉丁 via 与 deviare 给出 deviate 与 deviation。两半只在技术短语里相遇。

items.example: The Germanic root supplies the idea of standing firm.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「站稳」的意思。

items.structure: -ard (Germanic noun suffix, often pejorative or emphatic)
items.meaning: a person or thing marked by
items.example: The suffix forms the noun for a fixed rallying point.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成表示固定集合点的名词。

items.example: The French noun is the direct source of standard.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语名词是 standard 的直接来源。

items.meaning: a fixed rule or model; a banner
items.example: The standard was agreed in advance.
items.exampleCN: 标准是事先约定的。

items.example: The root supplies the road in deviation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供 deviation 里的「道路」。

items.meaning: to leave the road; to stray
items.example: The verb pictures stepping off a road.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词描绘离开道路的一步。

items.meaning: the act of straying from a course
items.example: The deviation was small.
items.exampleCN: 偏差很小。

items.example: Do not deviate from the plan.
items.exampleCN: 不要偏离计划。

items.example: A devious route avoids the checkpoint.
items.exampleCN: 绕行的路线避开了检查站。

definition_zh: 概率；可能性；或然性；概率论；可信度
definition_en: the extent to which something is likely to happen or to be true, or the branch of mathematics that measures it
core_image: 一只骰子在桌上翻滚，六面朝上的机会被写成一个分数
scene: 气象员看着云图，给出明天下雨的可能性很小。The probability of rain tomorrow is low.
sceneCN: 这里指「某件事发生的可能程度」（第 2 个义项：日常可能性）；句意为明天下雨的可能性很低。可辨识物件：云图、天气图、铅笔、概率标尺。

pos.zh: 概率；可能性；或然性；概率论

senses.title: A numerical measure of chance
senses.definition: a number between zero and one expressing how likely an event is
senses.definitionCN: 取值在零与一之间、表示事件可能程度的数
senses.example: The probability of drawing an ace is one in thirteen.
senses.exampleCN: 抽到王牌的概率是十三分之一。
senses.why: Latin probabilitas named credibility; mathematics narrowed it into a number between nought and one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 probabilitas 本指可信程度；数学把它收窄成零与一之间的一个数。

senses.title: The likelihood of an event
senses.definition: how likely something is to happen, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常说法里某件事发生的可能程度
senses.example: The probability of rain tomorrow is low.
senses.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很低。
senses.why: The everyday sense keeps the older meaning of what may reasonably be expected.
senses.whyCN: 日常义保留较古的意思：什么可以合理地预期。

senses.title: The branch of mathematics
senses.definition: the mathematical study of chance and random events
senses.definitionCN: 研究机会与随机事件的数学分支
senses.example: Probability grew out of games of chance in the seventeenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 概率论在十七世纪从赌博游戏里发展出来。
senses.why: The name of the measure became the name of the discipline that studies it.
senses.whyCN: 这个量的名称变成了研究它的学科的名称。

senses.title: Conditional probability
senses.definition: the chance of one event given that another event has occurred
senses.definitionCN: 在另一事件已发生的前提下，某一事件发生的可能
senses.example: Conditional probability changes when the first event is known.
senses.exampleCN: 已知第一个事件之后，条件概率就改变了。
senses.why: Knowledge of one event removes part of the sample space, so the measure is recalculated within what remains.
senses.whyCN: 知道一个事件发生会去掉部分样本空间，于是概率在剩下的范围里重算。

senses.title: A value used in significance testing
senses.definition: the chance of seeing data at least this extreme if the null hypothesis holds
senses.definitionCN: 在原假设成立时，看到至少这样极端的数据的机会
senses.example: A probability below the threshold led the team to reject the null hypothesis.
senses.exampleCN: 概率低于阈值，使研究团队否定了原假设。
senses.why: Testing turns probability into a decision rule: if the chance of the data is small, the assumption is doubted.
senses.whyCN: 检验把概率变成一条决策规则：若数据出现的机会很小，就怀疑那个前提。

senses.title: The phrase 'in all probability'
senses.definition: a fixed phrase meaning that something is almost certain
senses.definitionCN: 一个表示某事几乎确定的固定说法
senses.example: In all probability, the train will be late.
senses.exampleCN: 十有八九，这趟车会晚点。
senses.why: The phrase adds 'all' to the measure in order to say that the likelihood is very high.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法在概率前加「全部」，以表示可能程度非常高。

senses.title: A very small chance
senses.definition: a chance so small that it is worth naming as remote
senses.definitionCN: 小到值得称为「渺茫」的机会
senses.example: There is a probability, though a remote one, that the letter was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信有可能丢失，尽管机会渺茫。
senses.why: English can use the same noun for a low value as for a high one, with a qualifier to mark the scale.
senses.whyCN: 英语可以用同一个名词指低值，也可以指高值，只靠限定词标出高低。

senses.title: Credibility of a statement
senses.definition: the degree to which an account or a claim deserves belief
senses.definitionCN: 一种说法或主张值得相信的程度
senses.example: The probability of her account rests on two witnesses.
senses.exampleCN: 她的说法有多可信，取决于两位证人。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is exactly this: what is worthy of approval, before any number is attached.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层正是如此：什么值得认可，还没有附上任何数字。

intro.en: Probability comes from Latin probabilitas 'credibility', from probabilis 'that can be approved or proved', from probare 'to test, prove'. It reached English through Old French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: probability 出自拉丁 probabilitas「可信」，再上溯形容词 probabilis「可认可、可证明的」，动词为 probare「检验、证明」；十四世纪经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Probare meant 'to test, examine, prove'. It is related to probus 'good, upright', and the pair belongs to an old root of testing and approval, reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、审查、证明」。它与 probus「好、正直」相关，这一对词属于一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根为重构形式，并无直接书证。

items.en: Probus meant 'good, honest, upright', said of people and of quality. The link with probare is generally accepted, though the exact root shape is reconstructed.
items.cn: probus 意为「好、诚实、正直」，可用于人和品质。它与 probare 的联系一般被接受，但确切词根形态属重构。

items.en: Probabilis meant 'that can be approved, credible', and was used of opinions and evidence before it was used of numbers.
items.cn: probabilis 意为「可认可的、可信的」，先用于意见与证据，后用于数字。

items.en: The abstract noun probabilitas named the quality of being credible, the direct source of the English word.
items.cn: 抽象名词 probabilitas 指可信的性质，是英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French probabilite carried the noun into English in the fourteenth century, first in the sense of likelihood or plausibility.
items.cn: 古法语 probabilite 在十四世纪把这个名词带入英语，最初指「看似可能」。

items.en: The numerical sense developed with the mathematics of games of chance in the seventeenth century, and the discipline took the word as its name.
items.cn: 数值义随十七世纪赌博数学发展起来，这门学科也把这个词当作名称。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same proving root that are easy to confuse; group two holds words for how likely something is.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「检验、证明」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「有多大可能」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for something likely or credible; the noun is its abstract form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示很可能或可信的形容词；名词是它的抽象形式。

entries.definition: Able to be demonstrated by evidence; it comes from prove, which shares the Latin proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 可由证据证明的；出自与拉丁「证明」同根的 prove。

entries.definition: Evidence that settles a question; the noun of result from the same proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 能定论一个问题的证据；同根的结果名词。

entries.definition: Uprightness of character, from probus 'good'; it looks like probability but names a virtue.
entries.definitionCN: 品行的正直，出自 probus「好」；形似 probability，却指一种德性。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for the chance of something, with no mathematical claim.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事机会的日常名词，不带数学含义。

entries.definition: The possibility that something happens, often spoken informally.
entries.definitionCN: 某事发生的可能，常用于口语。

entries.definition: The ratio between the chances of two outcomes, as in betting.
entries.definitionCN: 两种结果机会之比，常用于博彩。

entries.definition: Something that can happen, with no statement about how often.
entries.definitionCN: 可能发生的事，不说明频率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'test and approve', so probability began as credibility and only later became a number.
normal.cn: 词根意为「检验与认可」，因此概率最初指可信，后来才变成数字。

normal.en: One family runs probability, probable, probably, probabilistic, improbable and probity.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：概率、很可能的、很可能、概率的、不太可能的、正直。

normal.en: The same proving root gives proof, prove and provable, all about evidence rather than chance.
normal.cn: 同一「证明」词根还给出证据、证明、可证明的，都关于证据而非机会。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: the probability of, in all probability, conditional probability.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：某事的概率、十有八九、条件概率。

normal.en: A probability is a number between nought and one; anything outside that range is not a probability at all.
normal.cn: 概率是零与一之间的数；超出这个范围的就不是概率。

abstract.en: Picture a die rolling across a table, with one face counted and written as a fraction.
abstract.cn: 想象一只骰子在桌上翻滚，某一面被数出来写成一个分数。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map with a shaded band whose width shows how unsure the forecaster is.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，上面一条带阴影的宽带显示预报员有多不确定。

abstract.en: Picture a jury weighing two witnesses, deciding how much credit a story deserves.
abstract.cn: 想象陪审团权衡两位证人，判断一个说法值多少信任。

examples.en: The probability of two heads in a row is one quarter.
examples.cn: 连续两次抛出正面的概率是四分之一。

examples.en: In all probability the meeting will end early.
examples.cn: 十有八九，会议会提前结束。

examples.en: Conditional probability depends on what is already known.
examples.cn: 条件概率取决于已知的情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「检验、证明」，加抽象名词词尾表示「可被认可的性质」：先指说法可信，后指数值化的机会大小。

root: 拉丁 probabilitas「可信」＝ probabilis「可认可的」＋抽象名词词尾，probabilis 出自 probare「检验、证明」，与 probus「正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根为重构形式。英语十四世纪经古法语传入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: something is weighed and found more or less worthy of belief. That weighing becomes a number, then a discipline, then a decision rule, and finally any estimate of how likely a claim is to be true.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：把某事放在天平上称一称，看它值多少信任。这种称量先变成数字，再变成学科，再变成决策规则，最后指对一种说法为真的可能程度的估计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a die rolling across a table while a shaded band on a weather map shows how unsure the answer is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只骰子在桌上翻滚，同时天气图上一条阴影带显示答案有多不确定。

branches.en: A NUMBER: the technical value and the everyday likelihood are one scale, read precisely or loosely.
branches.cn: 一个数：技术数值与日常可能程度是同一把尺，只是读得精或粗。

branches.en: A DISCIPLINE: the study of chance, including the case where part of the answer is already known.
branches.cn: 一门学科：研究机会，包括已知部分答案的情形。

branches.en: TEST RULE: a small probability of the data becomes grounds for doubting an assumption.
branches.cn: 检验规则：数据出现机会很小，就成了怀疑某个前提的理由。

branches.en: SCALE: the same noun can name a near certainty or a remote chance, with a qualifier to mark which end.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一个名词既可指近乎确定，也可指渺茫机会，靠限定词标出哪一端。

branches.en: CREDIBILITY: the oldest layer asks how much belief a statement deserves.
branches.cn: 可信度：最古老的一层问的是一种说法值多少相信。

intro.en: Probability is a Latin abstract noun from a verb of testing; the same root builds the adjectives and the plain verb for proving.
intro.cn: probability 是一个拉丁抽象名词，出自表示检验的动词；同一词根还构成形容词与表示证明的普通动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare gives probabilitas, probabilis and probus; the English family includes probable, proof, prove and probity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 probare 衍生 probabilitas、probabilis 与 probus；英语词族包括 probable、proof、prove、probity。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of testing something before believing it.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「先检验再相信」的意思。

items.example: The adjective adds a moral shade to the same root.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给同一词根加上道德色彩。

items.meaning: able to be approved or proved
items.example: The adjective names what passes the test.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指能通过检验的东西。

items.example: The noun names the quality, then the measure.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词先指性质，后指度量。

items.example: The probability is low.
items.exampleCN: 概率很低。

items.example: A storm is probable.
items.exampleCN: 很可能有风暴。

items.example: He will probably agree.
items.exampleCN: 他多半会同意。

items.example: Her probity was never doubted.
items.exampleCN: 她的正直从未被怀疑。

definition_zh: 很可能的；可信的；有理由的；有相当根据的
definition_en: likely to happen or to be true, or reasonable enough to be believed
core_image: 天平两端各放一份证据，装证据较多的一侧缓缓下沉
scene: 气象员指着西边压来的云层，判断傍晚前会有雷暴。A storm is probable by evening.
sceneCN: 这里指「很可能会发生的」（第 1 个义项：事件很可能发生）；句意为傍晚之前很可能有一场雷暴。可辨识物件：云层、风向标、雷达图、记录板。

pos.zh: 很可能的；可信的；有理由的

senses.title: Likely to happen
senses.definition: having a strong chance of happening
senses.definitionCN: 发生的可能性很大
senses.example: A storm is probable by evening.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚之前很可能有一场雷暴。
senses.why: The Latin adjective means 'that can be approved', and what can be approved is what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁形容词意为「可获认可的」，而可获认可的就是证据所支持的东西。

senses.title: Credible as an account
senses.definition: likely to be true, said of a story or an explanation
senses.definitionCN: 很可能为真，用于说法或解释
senses.example: Her version of events is probable, though not proved.
senses.exampleCN: 她对事情的描述很可信，尽管未获证明。
senses.why: The oldest sense concerns belief rather than events: a probable account is one worthy of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项关乎相信而非事件：可信的说法就是值得接受的说法。

senses.title: Supported by reasoning
senses.definition: resting on reasons that make it sensible to accept
senses.definitionCN: 有理由支撑，使接受它显得合理
senses.example: The simplest probable explanation is often the right one.
senses.exampleCN: 最简单的、说得通的解释往往就是对的。
senses.why: A conclusion is probable when the reasons for it outweigh the reasons against, a weighing rather than a proof.
senses.whyCN: 当支持的理由重于反对的理由，结论就是「说得通」的；这是称量，而非证明。

senses.title: Reasonable grounds in law
senses.definition: having enough evidence for an officer to act, in the fixed phrase probable cause
senses.definitionCN: 证据足以让执法人员采取行动，用于固定说法「合理根据」
senses.example: The search was allowed because there was probable cause.
senses.exampleCN: 由于存在合理根据，这次搜查获得准许。
senses.why: Law borrows the weighing image and asks whether the evidence is strong enough to justify action, not to convict.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了称量的形象，问的是证据是否足以支持行动，而不是足以定罪。

senses.title: Likely in a scientific estimate
senses.titleCN: 科学估计中的或然结论
senses.definition: likely according to a model or an estimate rather than a certainty
senses.definitionCN: 依模型或估计而言很可能，而非确定
senses.example: The probable range of the signal was published with the data.
senses.exampleCN: 信号的或然范围随数据一并发表。
senses.why: Science states results as probable ranges, keeping the word's sense of what the evidence supports.
senses.whyCN: 科学把结果说成或然范围，保留了「证据所支持」的意思。

senses.title: The expected winner
senses.definition: the competitor expected to win, in the phrase the probable winner
senses.definitionCN: 在固定说法中指被预期会赢的参赛者
senses.example: She was the probable winner before the final heat.
senses.exampleCN: 在最后一轮预赛之前，她是最被看好的人。
senses.why: Expectation based on evidence is the same weighing applied to a field of competitors.
senses.whyCN: 基于证据的预期，就是同一种称量用在参赛者身上。

senses.title: A probable opinion in moral theology
senses.definition: an opinion with solid support that may be followed without certainty, in the older theological use
senses.definitionCN: 有可靠依据、无需确定即可采纳的意见，属较早的神学用法
senses.example: The older manuals asked whether a probable opinion could safely be followed.
senses.exampleCN: 较早的手册会问：一个可采意见是否能被安全遵循。
senses.why: This technical sense keeps the Latin meaning exactly: an opinion that can be approved, even without proof.
senses.whyCN: 这个专门义精确保留拉丁原义：一种即使未获证明也可获认可的意见。

senses.title: Belief made reasonable by evidence
senses.titleCN: 抽象：证据使相信成为合理
senses.definition: the quality of a claim whose evidence makes belief reasonable
senses.definitionCN: 一种主张因证据而使相信显得合理的性质
senses.example: What makes the claim probable is not certainty but the weight of the evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 使这个主张可信的不是确定性，而是证据的分量。
senses.why: The abstract sense isolates the weighing itself, without naming an event, an account or a court.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义把称量本身单独提出来，不指事件、说法或法庭。

intro.en: Probable comes through Old French from Latin probabilis 'that can be approved or proved', an adjective from probare 'to test, prove'. It entered English in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: probable 经古法语来自拉丁形容词 probabilis「可认可、可证明的」，出自动词 probare「检验、证明」；十四世纪进入英语。

items.en: Probare meant 'to test, examine, prove'. It belongs with probus 'good, upright' to an old root of testing and approval; that root is reconstructed.
items.cn: probare 意为「检验、审查、证明」。它与 probus「好、正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根属重构形式。

items.en: Probabilis meant 'that can be approved, credible'. It described opinions and evidence long before it described events.
items.cn: probabilis 意为「可获认可的、可信的」，在用于事件之前，长期用于意见与证据。

items.en: Old French probable passed the adjective into English in the fourteenth century, where it first meant credible rather than likely to happen.
items.cn: 古法语 probable 在十四世纪把这个形容词带入英语，最初意为「可信」，而非「很可能发生」。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word was increasingly used of future events, so likelihood joined credibility.
items.cn: 从十六世纪起，这个词越来越多用于未来事件，于是「可能发生」与「可信」合并。

items.en: The legal phrase probable cause is a fixed term of art, and its earliest uses are dated only approximately.
items.cn: 法律短语「合理根据」是一个固定术语，其最早用例只能给出约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same proving root that are easily confused; group two holds words for what is likely or believable.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「证明」词根、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示「很可能」或「可信」的词。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for likelihood or credibility; the adjective is its descriptive form.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性或可信的抽象名词；形容词是它的描述形式。

entries.definition: Able to be demonstrated; it comes from prove, which shares the Latin proving root but stresses demonstration.
entries.definitionCN: 可被证明的；出自 prove，同享拉丁「证明」词根，但强调实证。

entries.definition: Tending to prove something, used of evidence in law.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于证明某事的，用于法律上的证据。

entries.definition: From plaudere 'to applaud': originally 'deserving applause', hence seemingly reasonable; it is not the proving root.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 plaudere「鼓掌」，原意「值得鼓掌」，引申为「看似有理」；与「证明」词根无关。

entries.definition: The everyday adjective for a strong chance, without the evidential weight that probable carries.
entries.definitionCN: 表示机会很大的日常形容词，不带 probable 那种证据分量。

entries.definition: From credere 'to believe': able to be believed, close to the older sense of probable.
entries.definitionCN: 出自 credere「相信」，意为「可被相信」，接近 probable 较古的义项。

entries.definition: Able to be accepted as true, often said of stories and excuses.
entries.definitionCN: 能被当作真实接受的，常用于说法与借口。

entries.definition: Anticipated as likely to occur, with less emphasis on evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 预期会发生，对证据的强调较少。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root means 'test and approve', so probable first meant believable and only later meant likely to happen.
normal.cn: 词根意为「检验与认可」，因此 probable 先指可信，后来才指很可能发生。

normal.en: One family runs probable, probably, probability, probabilistic, improbable and probity.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：很可能的、很可能、概率、概率的、不太可能的、正直。

normal.en: The legal phrase probable cause is a fixed term, not a free combination.
normal.cn: 法律短语「合理根据」是固定术语，不是可以随意组合的说法。

normal.en: Other words about proof are close relatives: prove, proof, provable, probative.
normal.cn: 其他关于证明的词是近亲：证明、证据、可证明的、有证明力的。

normal.en: Plausible looks like a relative but comes from applause, not from proof.
normal.cn: plausible 看似同族，实际出自「鼓掌」，与「证明」无关。

abstract.en: Picture two pans of evidence on a balance, the heavier one slowly winning.
abstract.cn: 想象天平两端各放一份证据，较重的一侧缓缓占上风。

abstract.en: Picture a witness whose story holds together under every question.
abstract.cn: 想象一位证人的说法在每一次追问下都站得住。

abstract.en: Picture a courtroom where the standard is enough evidence to act, not enough to convict.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法庭，标准是「足以行动的证据」，而非「足以定罪」。

examples.en: It is probable that the flight will be delayed.
examples.cn: 这趟航班很可能会延误。

examples.en: The police must show probable cause before a search.
examples.cn: 警方在搜查之前必须说明合理根据。

examples.en: The theory is probable but not yet proved.
examples.cn: 这个理论说得通，但尚未获得证明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 词根意为「检验、证明」，加形容词词尾表示「能被……的」：能被检验通过的，先是「可信」，后是「很可能」。

root: 拉丁 probabilis「可认可的」＝ probare「检验、证明」＋形容词词尾 -abilis，与 probus「正直」同属一个表示「检验与认可」的古老词根，该词根属重构形式。英语十四世纪经古法语传入，最初意为「可信」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act: evidence is weighed. When the heavier side carries belief, a statement is credible; when it carries expectation, an event is likely; law and science fix the threshold of action and of conclusion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把证据放到天平上称。较重的一侧支撑相信时，说法就可信；支撑预期时，事件就很可能；法律与科学则各自定出行动与结论的门槛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two pans of evidence on a balance, the heavier one slowly winning.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平两端各放着一份证据，较重的一侧缓缓占上风。

branches.en: WEIGH: likelihood and credibility are the same balance read toward the future or the past.
branches.cn: 称量：可能发生与可信，是天平朝未来或朝过去读的两个方向。

branches.en: REASON ENOUGH: when reasons outweigh counter-reasons, the conclusion is probable.
branches.cn: 理由足够：当支持的理由重于反对的理由，结论就是说得通的。

branches.en: THE BAR: the law asks only whether there is enough for action.
branches.cn: 门槛：法律只问证据是否足以行动。

branches.en: DISCIPLINE: science and older moral theology both fix what may be held without certainty.
branches.cn: 专门领域：科学与较早的道德神学都定出「无确定也可持有」的范围。

branches.en: EXPECTATION: evidence can also pick a likely winner, or simply make belief reasonable.
branches.cn: 预期：证据也能挑出被看好的人，或只是使相信显得合理。

intro.en: Probable is a Latin adjective from a verb of proving; the same root builds nouns of likelihood and the plain words for proof.
intro.cn: probable 是一个拉丁形容词，出自表示证明的动词；同一词根还构成表示可能性的名词与表示证据的普通词。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare and probus give probabilis, probabilitas and the English family probable, probability, prove and proof.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 probare 与 probus 衍生 probabilis、probabilitas，并给出英语词族 probable、probability、prove、proof。

items.example: The root supplies testing before acceptance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「先检验再接受」的意思。

items.example: The adjective adds moral approval to the same stock.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词给同一词源加上道德认可。

items.example: The adjective names what passes the test.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指能通过检验的东西。

items.example: A storm is probable.
items.exampleCN: 很可能有风暴。

items.example: Probably nobody noticed.
items.exampleCN: 大概没人注意到。

items.example: The probability is small.
items.exampleCN: 概率很小。

items.example: An improbable outcome.
items.exampleCN: 一个不太可能的结果。

items.example: Her probity was respected.
items.exampleCN: 她的正直受人敬重。

definition_zh: 概率的；或然性的；随机性的；基于概率模型的
definition_en: relating to probability, or based on chance rather than on certainty
core_image: 一张地图上许多可能的路径同时亮起，每条都标着一个可能性大小
scene: 模型给出的不是单一答案，而是一组带可能性的区间。The model gives a probabilistic forecast rather than a single number.
sceneCN: 这里指「以概率方式给出、不承诺单一确定结果」（第 1 个义项：概率性的）；句意为这个模型给出概率预报，而不是一个单值。可辨识物件：地图、多条路径、区间刻度、标注笔。

pos.zh: 概率的；或然性的；随机性的

senses.title: Expressed as a probability
senses.definition: stated as a probability rather than as a definite fact
senses.definitionCN: 以概率而非确定事实的方式陈述
senses.example: The model gives a probabilistic forecast rather than a single number.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型给出概率预报，而不是一个单值。
senses.why: The suffix turns probability into an adjective of method: the answer is a distribution, not a point.
senses.whyCN: 词尾把概率变成方法的形容词：答案是一组分布，而不是一个点。

senses.title: Based on a probability model
senses.definition: built on a model that assigns chances to outcomes
senses.definitionCN: 建立在为各种结果分配机会的模型之上
senses.example: A probabilistic model of traffic predicts delays by hour.
senses.exampleCN: 一个交通概率模型按小时预测延误。
senses.why: Modelling by chance means writing down a set of possible outcomes and their weights.
senses.whyCN: 用机会建模，就是写下各种可能结果及其权重。

senses.title: Random rather than fixed
senses.definition: depending on chance, with no single predetermined outcome
senses.definitionCN: 取决于机会，没有单一预定的结果
senses.example: The arrival times are probabilistic, so no schedule is exact.
senses.exampleCN: 到达时间具有随机性，因此没有一份时刻表是精确的。
senses.why: If the same cause can lead to different effects, the process is described by chances instead of by a rule.
senses.whyCN: 若同一原因可能导致不同结果，这个过程就用机会而非规则来描述。

senses.title: Belonging to probability theory
senses.definition: of or belonging to the mathematical theory of chance
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究机会的数学理论
senses.example: Probabilistic reasoning entered the curriculum last year.
senses.exampleCN: 概率推理去年被纳入课程。
senses.why: The adjective marks the branch of mathematics, not the everyday estimate.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出数学分支，而非日常估计。

senses.title: Weighing evidence by degrees
senses.definition: treating belief as a matter of degree supported by evidence
senses.definitionCN: 把相信当成由证据支持的程度问题
senses.example: The philosopher argued for a probabilistic reading of evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这位哲学家主张用一种按程度权衡证据的读法。
senses.why: Philosophy uses the word when belief is measured rather than simply held.
senses.whyCN: 当信念被度量而非简单持有时，哲学就用这个词。

senses.title: A method in machine learning
senses.titleCN: 机器学习中的概率方法
senses.definition: describing a learning system that outputs probabilities over possible answers
senses.definitionCN: 描述输出各种可能答案之概率的学习系统
senses.example: The classifier is probabilistic and reports its confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 这个分类器是概率式的，会报告它的置信度。
senses.why: A system that ranks answers by chance can say how unsure it is, which a fixed rule cannot.
senses.whyCN: 按机会给答案排序的系统能说出自己有多不确定，固定规则则不能。

senses.title: A chance-based public forecast
senses.definition: a public forecast given as chances, as in weather or risk reports
senses.definitionCN: 以机会形式发布的预报，如天气或风险报告
senses.example: The coastal warning was probabilistic, giving a range of chances.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警报是概率式的，给出一组机会值。
senses.why: Forecasters prefer chances because a single yes or no hides how uncertain the science is.
senses.whyCN: 预报员偏好机会值，因为单纯的「是」或「否」会掩盖科学上的不确定。

senses.title: Accepting uncertainty as the frame
senses.titleCN: 抽象：承认不确定的框架
senses.definition: a way of thinking that accepts uncertainty instead of demanding certainty
senses.definitionCN: 一种接受不确定、而不强求确定的思考方式
senses.example: A probabilistic outlook does not wait for perfect information.
senses.exampleCN: 概率式的眼光不会坐等完备的信息。
senses.why: The abstract sense is the stance itself: act on weighted chances rather than on certainty.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义就是这种立场本身：按加权机会行动，而非按确定性行动。

intro.en: Probabilistic is probability with the Greek-derived adjective ending -istic, which came to English through Latin -isticus. The word is a nineteenth-century formation.
intro.cn: probabilistic 是 probability 加一个源自希腊语、经拉丁 -isticus 传入英语的形容词词尾 -istic 构成；这个词是十九世纪的构词。

items.en: Probare 'to test, prove' is the base of the whole family; its old root of testing is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: probare「检验、证明」是整个词族的基础；其表示检验的古老词根属重构形式，并无直接书证。

items.en: Probabilitas 'credibility, likelihood' supplied the noun from which the adjective was made.
items.cn: probabilitas「可信、或然」提供了构成这个形容词的名词。

items.en: The ending -isticos in Greek formed adjectives of manner or practice; Latin -isticus and French -istique carried it into English as -istic.
items.cn: 希腊语词尾 -istikos 构成表示方式或实践活动的形容词；经拉丁 -isticus 与法语 -istique 进入英语，成为 -istic。

items.en: The adjective appears in the nineteenth century, when chance-based reasoning was being formalised in mathematics and philosophy.
items.cn: 这个形容词出现在十九世纪，正值以机会为基础的推理在数学与哲学中被形式化。

items.en: Twentieth-century statistics, computing and forecasting gave the word wide currency, especially in the phrase probabilistic model.
items.cn: 二十世纪的统计学、计算与预报使这个词广泛流行，尤见于「概率模型」这一说法。

items.en: The exact first citation is not firmly established; dictionary dates for the adjective are approximate.
items.cn: 确切的最早书证没有定论，词典给出的年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that merely look similar or belong to the same family; group two holds words for chance-based or uncertain approaches.
note.cn: 第一组是形似或同族的词；第二组是表示「基于机会」或「不确定」的进路。

entries.definition: An adverb of likelihood, not an adjective of method; it modifies a whole statement.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性的副词，而非方法的形容词；它修饰整个陈述。

entries.definition: From problema 'a thing put forward', a Greek word; it means difficult or doubtful, not chance-based.
entries.definitionCN: 出自希腊语 problema「被提出之物」；意为「成问题的」，与机会无关。

entries.definition: Tending to prove something, used of evidence rather than of models.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于证明某事的，用于证据而非模型。

entries.definition: The noun of chance from which the adjective is formed.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个形容词的「概率」名词。

entries.definition: A technical synonym for random or chance-governed, common in mathematics and finance.
entries.definitionCN: 表示随机或受机会支配的技术同义词，常见于数学与金融。

entries.definition: Relating to the analysis of data; it may use probabilities but does not have to.
entries.definitionCN: 关于数据分析的；可能用到概率，但不必然。

entries.definition: Lacking a predictable pattern, the plain everyday word.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏可预测的规律，是最朴素的日常说法。

entries.definition: Not known or not fixed, with no claim of a measured chance.
entries.definitionCN: 未知或未定，不声称量出了机会。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the noun of chance plus an adjective ending meaning 'in the manner of'.
normal.cn: 这个词是「概率」名词加一个表示「以……方式」的形容词词尾。

normal.en: One family runs probability, probable, probably, probabilistic, probabilistically and probabilism.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：概率、很可能的、很可能、概率的、按概率方式地、或然论。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the technical uses: probabilistic model, probabilistic forecast, probabilistic reasoning.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出技术用法：概率模型、概率预报、概率推理。

normal.en: Problematic begins with the same letters but comes from a Greek word for something put forward, not from proof.
normal.cn: problematic 开头字母相同，却出自希腊语「被提出之物」，与证明无关。

normal.en: An answer given as a range of chances can state its own uncertainty; a single yes cannot.
normal.cn: 以一组机会给出的答案能说出自己的不确定；单纯的「是」不能。

abstract.en: Picture a map with several possible routes lit at once, each carrying a small weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上同时亮起几条可能的路，每条都带一个小权重。

abstract.en: Picture a weather band whose width is the message, not the line down its middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一条天气带，它的宽度才是信息，中间的线不是。

abstract.en: Picture a sailor who plans for several winds at once instead of betting on one.
abstract.cn: 想象一位水手同时为几种风做准备，而不是只押一种。

examples.en: The team built a probabilistic model of river flooding.
examples.cn: 团队建立了一个河流泛滥的概率模型。

examples.en: Probabilistic reasoning accepts degrees of belief.
examples.cn: 概率推理接受信念有程度之分。

examples.en: The forecast was probabilistic, with a wide range of chances.
examples.cn: 这次预报是概率式的，机会值范围很宽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 名词表示「概率」，形容词词尾表示「以……为方式」：合起来就是「按机会大小来说、不承诺单一结果」的做法。

root: probability 加源自希腊语 -istikos、经拉丁 -isticus 传入的形容词词尾；probability 出自拉丁 probabilitas，再上溯 probare「检验、证明」，其古老词根属重构形式。这个词是十九世纪的构词，确切首见年代为约数。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses describe one stance: answers are given as weighted chances. The stance appears in a forecast, in a model, in randomness, in a theory, in philosophy, in machine learning, in public warnings, and finally as a way of acting without certainty.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项描述同一种立场：答案以加权机会的形式给出。这种立场依次出现在预报、模型、随机过程、数学理论、哲学、机器学习、公共警报，最后成为一种「不确定也行动」的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several possible routes lit at once on one map, each carrying a weight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张地图上同时亮起几条可能的路，每条都带一个权重。

branches.en: FORECAST: a public warning and a model output both state chances instead of one answer.
branches.cn: 预报：公共警报与模型输出都以机会陈述，而不给单一答案。

branches.en: MODEL: a chance model and a learning system both rank outcomes by weight.
branches.cn: 模型：机会模型与学习系统都按权重给结果排序。

branches.en: NO FIXED ROUTE: when one cause can yield different effects, chances replace a rule.
branches.cn: 无定路：当同一原因能产生不同结果，机会就代替了规则。

branches.en: THEORY AND BELIEF: mathematics and philosophy both treat belief as a degree.
branches.cn: 理论与信念：数学与哲学都把相信当成一种程度。

branches.en: THE STANCE: acting on weighted chances rather than waiting for certainty.
branches.cn: 立场：按加权机会行动，而非坐等确定。

intro.en: Probabilistic is a noun of chance plus an adjective ending of Greek origin, carried into English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: probabilistic 是一个表示机会的名词加一个源自希腊语的形容词词尾，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin probare gives probability; Greek -istikos, through Latin -isticus, gives the ending -istic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 probare 给出 probability；希腊语 -istikos 经拉丁 -isticus 给出词尾 -istic。

items.example: The root supplies the testing of evidence.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供对证据的检验。

items.example: The noun supplies the idea of measured chance.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「被度量的机会」这一观念。

items.structure: -istic (adjective suffix from Greek -istikos, 'in the manner of')
items.meaning: in the manner of; relating to
items.example: The suffix turns the noun into an adjective of method.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成方法的形容词。

items.example: Probability can be estimated.
items.exampleCN: 概率可以被估计。

items.example: A probabilistic model was used.
items.exampleCN: 使用了一个概率模型。

items.example: The claim was assessed probabilistically.
items.exampleCN: 这个主张按概率方式被评估。

items.meaning: the doctrine that probability guides action
items.example: Probabilism allowed a probable opinion to be followed.
items.exampleCN: 或然论允许遵循一个有依据的意见。

items.meaning: one who holds a probabilistic view
items.example: The probabilist defended the weaker claim.
items.exampleCN: 这位或然论者为较弱的那个主张辩护。

definition_zh: 统计学；统计数据；统计资料；统计量
definition_en: the science of collecting and analysing numerical data, or the data so collected
core_image: 一张大表被逐行汇总成几根柱子和一条曲线，边上写着总人数
scene: 年报用大量数字说明过去一年的变化。The statistics show a steady decline in rainfall.
sceneCN: 这里指「汇总起来的统计数据」（第 2 个义项：统计数据）；句意为这些统计数据显示降雨量持续下降。可辨识物件：年报、数据表、柱状图、计算器。

pos.zh: 统计学（作单数）；统计数据（作复数）；统计资料

senses.title: The science of numerical data
senses.definition: the branch of mathematics that collects, summarises and analyses data
senses.definitionCN: 收集、汇总与分析数据的数学分支
senses.example: Statistics is taught as a separate subject in the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 统计学在第二年作为独立科目教授。
senses.why: The discipline takes a plural form but a singular verb, because the name of a field is treated as one subject.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科形式上是复数，动词却用单数，因为学科名称被当作一个整体。

senses.title: Numerical data collected
senses.definition: sets of numbers gathered about a population or an activity
senses.definitionCN: 关于某个群体或某项活动收集起来的一组组数字
senses.example: The statistics show a steady decline in rainfall.
senses.exampleCN: 这些统计数据显示降雨量持续下降。
senses.why: The same form names the data as well as the study: what the discipline produces is called by its name.
senses.whyCN: 同一形式既指学科也指数据：学科产出的东西就以学科命名。

senses.title: Official published figures
senses.definition: figures regularly published by a government or an agency
senses.definitionCN: 政府或机构定期发布的数字
senses.example: The official statistics are revised every quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 官方统计数据每季度修订一次。
senses.why: Public numbers carry authority, so the word often means the official series rather than any calculation.
senses.whyCN: 公开的数字带有权威，因此这个词常指官方序列，而非任何计算。

senses.title: The use of statistical methods
senses.definition: the application of statistical methods to a question
senses.definitionCN: 把统计方法用到某个问题上
senses.example: The paper's statistics are sound but its sampling is weak.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文的统计处理可靠，取样却较弱。
senses.why: Judging a study means judging how its numbers were handled, and the word covers that handling.
senses.whyCN: 评价一项研究就是评价它的数字如何被处理，这个词覆盖那套处理。

senses.title: A table of summary figures
senses.definition: a table or set of summary figures presented together
senses.definitionCN: 一起呈现的一张汇总表或一组汇总数字
senses.example: The appendix prints the statistics by region.
senses.exampleCN: 附录按地区列出了这些统计数字。
senses.why: Collected numbers are usually presented as a table, and the table itself comes to be called the statistics.
senses.whyCN: 收集来的数字通常以表格呈现，表格本身也就被称作统计数据。

senses.title: Performance figures in sport
senses.definition: recorded numbers describing players' or teams' performance
senses.definitionCN: 记录球员或球队表现的数字
senses.example: His statistics improved sharply after the coaching change.
senses.exampleCN: 换教练之后，他的数据大幅提升。
senses.why: Sport applies the word to any counted record, especially when it is used to judge performance.
senses.whyCN: 体育把这个词用于任何计数记录，尤其当它被用来评判表现时。

senses.title: A single computed value
senses.definition: one computed value such as an average or a rate, in the singular form
senses.definitionCN: 以单数形式出现的一个计算值，如平均值或比率
senses.example: One statistic stands out: the median age has doubled.
senses.exampleCN: 有一个数字很突出：年龄中位数翻了一番。
senses.why: English keeps a singular form for one item and reserves the plural for the whole set.
senses.whyCN: 英语为一个条目保留单数形式，把复数留给整组数据。

senses.title: A way of describing a population by numbers
senses.definition: the practice of describing a whole population through counted features
senses.definitionCN: 通过计数特征来描述整个群体的做法
senses.example: Statistics turns a crowd into a shape one can compare with another crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 统计把一群人变成一个可以与他人比较的形状。
senses.why: The abstract sense names the move from many individuals to one describable profile.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义指从许多个体走向一个可描述轮廓的那一步。

intro.en: Statistics comes from German Statistik, a word coined in the eighteenth century for the systematic description of a state, from New Latin statisticum 'of state affairs' and Latin status 'state, condition'.
intro.cn: statistics 出自德语 Statistik，这个词在十八世纪被造出来，指对一个国家状况的系统描述；再上溯新拉丁 statisticum「国家事务的」与拉丁 status「状态、状况」。

items.en: Status meant 'standing, condition, state'. It comes from stare 'to stand', a verb of long standing in Latin.
items.cn: status 意为「处境、状况、状态」，出自 stare「站立」，这是一个在拉丁语中由来已久的动词。

items.en: The phrase statisticum collegium, a course on state affairs, supplied the adjective from which the German noun was formed.
items.cn: 短语 statisticum collegium 指关于国家事务的课程，提供了构成德语名词的形容词。

items.en: The German noun Statistik was coined in the eighteenth century for the systematic description of a state's resources and people.
items.cn: 德语名词 Statistik 在十八世纪被造出，指对国家资源与人口的系统描述。

items.en: English adopted statistics in the late eighteenth century, at first for the descriptive study of states and only later for numerical methods in general.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪末采用 statistics，最初指对国家的描述性研究，后来才泛指数值方法。

items.en: The plural ending survives from the German and Latin forms, but the discipline is treated as singular while the data remain plural.
items.cn: 复数词尾来自德语与拉丁形式，但这门学科被当作单数，而数据仍作复数。

items.en: The modern sense of analysing variation and probability is a nineteenth-century growth; early dates for particular uses are approximate.
items.cn: 分析变异与概率的现代义是十九世纪的发展；各个具体用法的早期年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives of the same word; group two holds words for the numbers themselves or for the study of them.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是表示数字本身或研究它们的词。

entries.definition: The singular form for a single computed value, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 单数形式，指一个计算值，而不是这门学科。

entries.definition: Relating to statistics or to methods of analysis.
entries.definitionCN: 关于统计学或分析方法的形容词。

entries.definition: A person who works with statistics, formed with the personal ending -ian.
entries.definitionCN: 从事统计工作的人，由表示人的词尾构成。

entries.definition: The plural form takes a singular verb for the subject and a plural verb for the data, a classic trap.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式用于学科时接单数动词，用于数据时接复数动词，是常见陷阱。

entries.definition: Collected observations before analysis; statistics is the analysis of such data.
entries.definitionCN: 分析之前的原始观察；统计学就是对这类数据的分析。

entries.definition: Numerical results as printed or quoted, with no claim of method.
entries.definitionCN: 印出或引用的数值结果，不涉及方法。

entries.definition: A set of chosen measures used to judge performance, common in business.
entries.definitionCN: 一组用来评判表现的选定度量，常用于商业。

entries.definition: The mathematics of chance, on which much of statistics rests.
entries.definitionCN: 关于机会的数学，统计学大量依赖它。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word began as a description of the state, which is why its oldest relative is the word for condition and standing.
normal.cn: 这个词最初是「对国家状况的描述」，因此它最古老的亲属词是表示「状况、处境」的词。

normal.en: One family runs statistics, statistic, statistical, statistically and statistician.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：统计学、统计量、统计的、从统计上看、统计学家。

normal.en: Remember the number agreement: the subject takes a singular verb, the data take a plural one.
normal.cn: 记住单复数搭配：指学科用单数动词，指数据用复数动词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: official statistics, vital statistics, the statistics show.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：官方统计数据、人口动态统计、统计数据显示。

normal.en: A single value is a statistic; the whole set or the science is statistics.
normal.cn: 一个数值是「统计量」，整组数据或这门学问是「统计学」。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of figures shrinking into three bars and one smooth curve.
abstract.cn: 想象一张长长的数字表缩成三根柱子和一条平滑曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of people replaced by a single outline that can be compared with another crowd.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人被一个轮廓替代，而这个轮廓能与另一群人相比。

abstract.en: Picture a government office printing the same table every quarter, whatever the weather.
abstract.cn: 想象一个政府办公室每季度印出同一张表，无论晴雨。

examples.en: Statistics is compulsory for students in this programme.
examples.cn: 统计学是这个项目的必修课。

examples.en: The statistics were collected over five years.
examples.cn: 这些统计数据是五年间收集的。

examples.en: One statistic surprised the panel: the rate had doubled.
examples.cn: 有一个数字让评审组吃惊：比率翻了一番。

dict_mnemonic.text: 这个词最初指「对国家状况的系统描述」，词根是表示「状态、处境」的拉丁词；后来从描述国家转到描述任何群体的数字，学科与数据都用同一个形式。

root: 德语 Statistik（十八世纪造词，指对国家状况的系统描述）经新拉丁 statisticum「国家事务的」上溯拉丁 status「状态、处境」，status 出自 stare「站立」。英语十八世纪末采用，先指国家描述，后泛指数值分析。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: many separate facts are turned into a few numbers that describe a whole. The movement is then called a science, a set of published figures, a method, a table, a player's record and, at last, a way of seeing a population.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把许多分散的事实变成少数描述整体的数字。这个动作再依次被称为一门学科、一组公布的数字、一种方法、一张表、一名球员的记录，最后成为看一个群体的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long table of figures shrinking into a few bars and one curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张长长的数字表缩成几根柱子和一条曲线。

branches.en: THE SCIENCE: the discipline collects and analyses numbers by fixed rules.
branches.cn: 学科：这门学问按固定规则收集与分析数字。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: collected data and the table that presents them share the name.
branches.cn: 数字：收集的数据与呈现它们的表格共用同一个名称。

branches.en: PUBLISHED RECORDS: official series and sports records are both counted and quoted.
branches.cn: 公布的记录：官方序列与体育记录都是被计数并被引用的。

branches.en: THE UNIT: methods handle numbers, and one computed value is a statistic.
branches.cn: 单位：方法处理数字，而一个计算值就是一个统计量。

branches.en: THE VIEW: the same move turns a crowd into one profile that can be compared with another.
branches.cn: 眼光：同一个动作把一群人变成一个可以与他人比较的轮廓。

intro.en: Statistics is a German coinage on a Latin base, and the family splits into the science, a single value, the adjective and the person.
intro.cn: statistics 是一个以拉丁语为底、在德语中造出的词；词族分成学科、单个值、形容词与从业者。

latinIntro.en: Latin status 'state, standing' gives statisticum and German Statistik; English adds statistic, statistical and statistician.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 status「状态、处境」给出 statisticum 与德语 Statistik；英语再加 statistic、statistical、statistician。

items.example: The root names the state being described.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指被描述的那个状态。

definition_zh: 统计学家；统计工作者；统计官员；数据统计人员
definition_en: a person who studies or applies statistics, or who prepares official statistical figures
core_image: 一个人伏在长桌前，把成叠的记录本一页页录入表格，再画出几条曲线
scene: 试验开始之前，一位统计学家检查了抽样方案是否合理。A statistician checked the sampling design before the trial began.
sceneCN: 这里指「以统计方法为专业的人」（第 1 个义项：统计学家）；句意为一位统计学家在试验开始前审查了抽样设计。可辨识物件：记录本、表格、计算器、抽样清单。

pos.zh: 统计学家；统计工作者；统计官员

senses.title: A researcher in statistics
senses.definition: a person who develops or studies statistical theory and methods
senses.definitionCN: 发展或研究统计理论与方法的人
senses.example: A statistician checked the sampling design before the trial began.
senses.exampleCN: 一位统计学家在试验开始前审查了抽样设计。
senses.why: The personal ending -ian marks a practitioner of the field named by the base word.
senses.whyCN: 表示人的词尾标出一个以该学科为业的人。

senses.title: A practitioner in industry
senses.definition: a person employed to apply statistical methods to practical problems
senses.definitionCN: 受雇把统计方法用于实际问题的人
senses.example: The company hired a statistician to review its quality data.
senses.exampleCN: 公司聘用了一位统计人员来审查质量数据。
senses.why: Industry needs the methods more than the theory, so the same title covers applied work.
senses.whyCN: 工业更需要方法而非理论，因此同一个头衔也覆盖应用工作。

senses.title: A government statistical officer
senses.definition: an official who prepares or publishes state figures
senses.definitionCN: 编制或发布国家数字的官员
senses.example: The official statistician signed the annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 官方统计人员签署了年度报告。
senses.why: The word grew up beside the description of states, and the official role keeps that oldest setting.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与国家描述一同成长，官方职位保留了最古老的场景。

senses.title: A biostatistician in trials
senses.titleCN: 临床试验中的生物统计师
senses.definition: a statistician who designs and analyses medical studies
senses.definitionCN: 设计并分析医学研究的统计人员
senses.example: The biostatistician set the rule for stopping the trial early.
senses.exampleCN: 生物统计师定下了提前终止试验的规则。
senses.why: Medicine needs a specialist to judge evidence, so the field grows a compound title with its own duties.
senses.whyCN: 医学需要专人来判断证据，于是这一行发展出带专门职责的复合头衔。

senses.title: An actuarial statistician
senses.definition: a statistician who estimates risk for insurers or pension funds
senses.definitionCN: 为保险公司或养老基金估计风险的统计人员
senses.example: An actuarial statistician modelled the claims for the next decade.
senses.exampleCN: 一位精算统计人员为今后十年的理赔建模。
senses.why: Risk pricing is an old statistical trade, and the title marks the person who does it.
senses.whyCN: 为风险定价是一门古老的统计行业，这个头衔标出做这件事的人。

senses.title: A sports statistician
senses.definition: a person who records and interprets performance figures in sport
senses.definitionCN: 记录并解读体育表现数字的人
senses.example: The team's statistician tracked every pass in the match.
senses.exampleCN: 球队的统计员记录了比赛中的每一次传球。
senses.why: Where performance is counted, someone is employed to keep the count, and the name follows the task.
senses.whyCN: 凡表现被计数的地方，就有人受雇维持这份计数，名称也随之而来。

senses.title: A data analyst in modern usage
senses.titleCN: 现代用法中的数据统计人员
senses.definition: a person whose work is largely statistical even if the job title differs
senses.definitionCN: 工作实质以统计为主、即使职位名称不同的人
senses.example: The job advert asked for a statistician who could code.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘启事要招一位会写程序的统计人员。
senses.why: The title has widened with computing, since the same methods now run on large datasets.
senses.whyCN: 随着计算技术发展，这个头衔变宽了，因为同样的方法如今跑在大数据集上。

senses.title: A teacher or consultant in statistics
senses.definition: a person who teaches the subject or advises others on its use
senses.definitionCN: 教授这门学科、或就它的使用向他人提供建议的人
senses.example: They brought in a statistician to explain the results to the board.
senses.exampleCN: 他们请来一位统计人员向董事会解释结果。
senses.why: Explaining numbers to non-specialists is part of the trade, so teaching and advice fall under the same name.
senses.whyCN: 向非专业者解释数字也是这一行的一部分，因此教学与咨询都归在同一个名称下。

intro.en: Statistician is statistics with the personal ending -ian, which English borrows from Latin adjectives in -ianus. The word appears in the nineteenth century as the subject took shape.
intro.cn: statistician 是 statistics 加表示人的词尾 -ian 构成，这个结尾源自拉丁语以 -ianus 结尾的形容词。这个词随学科成形，出现在十九世纪。

items.en: Status 'standing, condition' is the base of the whole family, and it comes from stare 'to stand'.
items.cn: status「处境、状况」是整个词族的基础，出自 stare「站立」。

items.en: German Statistik named the systematic description of a state, and English borrowed it late in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 德语 Statistik 指对国家状况的系统描述，英语在十八世纪末借入。

items.en: The English noun first meant the descriptive study of states, then the numerical analysis of any data.
items.cn: 这个英语名词先指对国家的描述性研究，后指对任何数据的数值分析。

items.en: -ianus in Latin formed adjectives of belonging, and English turns such adjectives into personal nouns with -ian.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ianus 构成表示归属的形容词，英语把这类形容词变为以 -ian 结尾的人物名词。

items.en: Statistician appears as the discipline acquires practitioners with a recognised title; exact first citations are approximate.
items.cn: statistician 随这门学科出现而出现，从业者有了公认头衔；确切的最早书证只是约数。

items.en: Computing and applied fields widened the title in the twentieth century, though the dictionary sense remains the statistical specialist.
items.cn: 二十世纪的计算与应用领域使这个头衔变宽，但词典义仍是统计专门人才。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same statistics base; group two holds neighbouring job titles and specialists.
note.cn: 第一组是建立在同一 statistics 词基上的形式；第二组是邻近的职称与专门人才。

entries.definition: The name of the discipline, which takes a singular verb when it means the subject.
entries.definitionCN: 学科名称；指这门学科时接单数动词。

entries.definition: A single computed number, not a person and not the science.
entries.definitionCN: 一个计算出来的数值，既不是人，也不是学科。

entries.definition: Relating to statistics, with no reference to a person.
entries.definitionCN: 关于统计学的形容词，不指人。

entries.definition: By statistical means, as in statistically significant.
entries.definitionCN: 以统计方式，如「统计上显著」。

entries.definition: A person who interprets data, often without formal statistical training.
entries.definitionCN: 解读数据的人，未必受过正式统计训练。

entries.definition: A specialist who calculates insurance and pension risk, traditionally from the same mathematical stock.
entries.definitionCN: 计算保险与养老风险的专业人士，传统上出自同一数学渊源。

entries.definition: A person who studies the spread of disease in populations, a heavy user of statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 研究疾病在人群中传播的人，重度依赖统计学。

entries.definition: A person who studies populations and their structure, using many statistical figures.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人口及其结构的人，使用大量统计数字。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The word is the field plus the personal ending, so it means the person who works with the field.
normal.cn: 这个词是学科名加表示人的词尾，因此指以这门学科为业的人。

normal.en: One family runs statistics, statistic, statistical, statistically and statistician.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：统计学、统计量、统计的、从统计上看、统计学家。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the roles: medical statistician, official statistician, chief statistician.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出角色：医学统计学家、官方统计人员、首席统计师。

normal.en: The oldest setting is the state: the title grew beside the description of a country's people and resources.
normal.cn: 最古老的场景是国家：这个头衔与国家人口资源的描述一同成长。

normal.en: The ending is the same one that turns a subject into a person, as in musician or historian.
normal.cn: 这个词尾与把学科变成人的词尾相同，如同音乐家或历史学家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 学科名加表示人的词尾：从事这门学问的人。它的词根原指「国家的状态」，因此最早的一批这样的人是在描述国家的人口与资源。

root: statistics 加表示人物的词尾 -ian（源自拉丁 -ianus）；statistics 出德语 Statistik（十八世纪造词），再上溯新拉丁 statisticum 与拉丁 status「状态、处境」，status 出自 stare「站立」。十九世纪出现，确切首见年代为约数。

branches.en: THE TRADE: research, industry and modern data work all apply the same methods.
branches.cn: 行业：研究、工业与现代数据工作都应用同样的方法。

branches.cn: 国家：最古老的场景是对一个国家的官方描述。

branches.en: THE RECORD: wherever performance is counted, someone keeps the count.

branches.en: THE ADVICE: teaching and consulting turn the trade outward.

definition_zh: 正态分布；高斯分布；钟形分布；标准正态分布
definition_en: a continuous probability distribution whose values cluster symmetrically around a mean, forming a bell-shaped curve
core_image: 一座左右对称的钟形山丘，正中最高，向两侧缓缓落平
scene: 测量数据大多聚在中间，越往两端越少，形成一条对称的曲线。Most measurements in the sample follow a normal distribution.
sceneCN: 这里指「数值围绕平均值对称聚集、两端渐稀的那种分布」（第 1 个义项：正态分布）；句意为样本中的大多数测量值服从正态分布。可辨识物件：坐标轴、对称曲线、中心线、刻度。

pos.zh: 正态分布；高斯分布；钟形分布

senses.title: The symmetric probability distribution
senses.definition: a continuous distribution in which values cluster symmetrically about a mean
senses.definitionCN: 数值围绕平均值对称聚集的连续分布
senses.example: Most measurements in the sample follow a normal distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 样本中大多数测量值服从正态分布。
senses.why: The curve rises to a single peak at the mean and falls away equally on both sides, which is why the name speaks of a rule or pattern.
senses.whyCN: 曲线在平均值处升到唯一的峰，两侧对称下落，因此这个名称说的是某种「规矩」或「范式」。

senses.title: The bell-shaped curve
senses.definition: the graph of such a distribution, shaped like a bell
senses.definitionCN: 这种分布的图形，形状像一口钟
senses.example: The data were plotted as a smooth bell curve.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据被画成一条平滑的钟形曲线。
senses.why: Plotting the distribution produces a curve whose outline is easy to recognise, so the picture often replaces the definition.
senses.whyCN: 画出分布就得到一条轮廓易认的曲线，于是图形常代替定义。

senses.title: The standard normal distribution
senses.definition: the special case with a mean of zero and a standard deviation of one
senses.definitionCN: 平均值为零、标准差为一的特例
senses.example: Tables of the standard normal distribution give areas under the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 标准正态分布表给出曲线下的面积。
senses.why: Setting the centre to zero and the spread to one makes every such curve comparable, so one table serves all cases.
senses.whyCN: 把中心定为零、离散定为一，就能让所有这类曲线可比，于是一张表可通用于全部情形。

senses.title: The Gaussian distribution
senses.definition: the same distribution under the name of Gauss, who studied its errors
senses.definitionCN: 同一分布以高斯之名称呼，他研究过其中的误差
senses.example: The Gaussian distribution appears in his work on astronomical errors.
senses.exampleCN: 高斯分布出现在他关于天文误差的研究中。
senses.why: A second name honours an early user rather than describing the shape; both names refer to one object.
senses.whyCN: 另一个名称纪念一位早期使用者，而不是描述形状；两个名称指同一个对象。

senses.title: The model for measurement errors
senses.definition: the assumed distribution of random errors around a true value
senses.definitionCN: 随机误差围绕真值分布的假设模型
senses.example: Repeated readings spread in a normal distribution around the true weight.
senses.exampleCN: 重复读数围绕真实重量呈正态分布散开。
senses.why: Errors small and large cancel in a way that produces a symmetric curve, which is why measurement adopted this model.
senses.whyCN: 大大小小的误差以一种方式相互抵消，产生对称曲线，测量学因此采用这个模型。

senses.title: The limiting distribution in the central limit theorem
senses.titleCN: 中心极限定理中的极限分布
senses.definition: the distribution that sums of many independent values approach
senses.definitionCN: 许多独立数值之和所趋近的分布
senses.example: Sums of many independent shocks approach a normal distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 许多独立冲击之和趋近正态分布。
senses.why: Adding many independent contributions smooths away their individual shapes, leaving the same symmetric curve, which explains how widely it appears.
senses.whyCN: 把许多独立贡献相加会抹平各自的形状，只剩同一条对称曲线，这解释了它为何到处出现。

senses.title: The object of normality tests
senses.definition: the pattern that data are compared with in a test of normality
senses.definitionCN: 正态性检验中用来与数据比较的那种模式
senses.example: The normality test asked whether the residuals were close enough to a normal distribution.
senses.exampleCN: 正态性检验问的是：残差是否足够接近正态分布。
senses.why: Because methods often assume the distribution, checking whether data resemble it became a standard step.
senses.whyCN: 由于方法常以此分布为前提，检查数据是否像它就成了标准步骤。

senses.title: The abstract shape of clustering at the centre
senses.titleCN: 抽象：居中密集、两端稀少的形态
senses.definition: any pattern in which most things sit near the middle and few at the edges
senses.definitionCN: 任何多数靠中间、少数在边缘的形态
senses.example: Awards in that field follow a normal distribution, with most near the middle.
senses.exampleCN: 那个领域的奖项呈正态分布，多数落在中间。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps only the silhouette, applying the bell to anything that thins out at both ends.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义只保留轮廓，把这口钟用在任何两端渐稀的事物上。

intro.en: Normal distribution joins Latin norma 'a carpenter's square, a rule' and Latin distribuere 'to allot'. The mathematical phrase took shape in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: normal distribution 由拉丁 norma「木匠的曲尺、规矩」与拉丁 distribuere「分配」合成；这个数学短语在十九世纪成形。

items.en: Norma meant a carpenter's square, and so a rule or a pattern. Its further origin is uncertain, and any older root suggested for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: norma 指木匠的曲尺，因此也指规矩、范式。其更早来源不确定，凡为其拟出的更古老词根都属假说。

items.en: Normalis meant 'made according to a square', hence right-angled and then regular, conforming to a rule.
items.cn: normalis 意为「按曲尺做成的」，因此指直角，再引申为合规矩、合乎范式。

items.en: Tribuere 'to allot, assign' is generally connected with tribus 'tribe', from the practice of assigning by tribe; the origin of tribus itself is not settled.
items.cn: tribuere「分配、分派」一般认为与 tribus「部族」有关，源于按部族分派的做法；tribus 本身的来源尚无定论。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus tribuere gave distribuere 'to divide up, distribute', and distributio named the division.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 tribuere 构成 distribuere「分给、分配」，名词 distributio 指这种分配。

items.en: The phrase normal distribution emerged in the nineteenth century as error theory and statistics converged; Gauss studied the error curve, and the adjective normal became standard in the 1890s.
items.cn: 这个短语在十九世纪随误差理论与统计学的汇合而出现；高斯研究过误差曲线，而形容词「正常的」在十九世纪九十年代成为标准叫法。

items.en: Gaussian distribution and bell curve are alternative names with their own histories; exact first citations for the English phrase vary, so dates here are approximate.
items.cn: 高斯分布与钟形曲线是各有来历的别名；这个英语短语的确切首见书证各有出入，此处年代只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds names and near-relatives of the same distribution; group two holds other distributions and words for spread.
note.cn: 第一组是同一分布的名称与近亲；第二组是其他分布以及表示离散的词。

entries.definition: An older and more descriptive name for the graph of the distribution, stressing the outline rather than the probability law.
entries.definitionCN: 较旧也更具描述性的名称，指这条曲线本身，强调轮廓而非概率规律。

entries.definition: The case with mean zero and standard deviation one, used to compare all others.
entries.definitionCN: 平均值为零、标准差为一的特例，用来比较其他所有情形。

entries.definition: The distribution of a variable whose logarithm is normal; it is skewed, not symmetric.
entries.definitionCN: 某个变量的对数服从正态分布时该变量的分布；它是偏斜的，并不对称。

entries.definition: The use of the normal curve to approximate another distribution, as with large samples.
entries.definitionCN: 用正态曲线近似另一种分布的方法，如大样本情形。

entries.definition: The same object named after Gauss, common in physics and engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 同一对象以高斯命名，常见于物理与工程。

entries.definition: The everyday name for the shape, often used outside technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 这种形状的日常叫法，常用于技术写作之外。

entries.definition: The distribution of the number of successes in fixed trials, discrete rather than continuous.
entries.definitionCN: 固定次数试验中成功次数的分布，是离散的而非连续的。

entries.definition: The distribution of counts of rare events in a fixed interval.
entries.definitionCN: 固定区间内稀有事件计数的分布。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The first word means 'according to a rule', the second means 'a dividing up': a regular way of spreading values.
normal.cn: 前一个词意为「合乎规矩」，后一个词意为「分配」：一种有规律的数值铺开方式。

normal.en: One family runs normal, normality, normalize, normally distributed and distribution.
normal.cn: 同族词串成一条线：正常的、正态性、使标准化、呈正态分布的、分布。

normal.en: Two names point at one object: the descriptive bell curve and the honorific Gaussian distribution.
normal.cn: 两个名称指同一个对象：描述形状的钟形曲线，与纪念高斯的正态分布。

normal.en: The special case with centre zero and spread one is the standard normal, the one tables are printed for.
normal.cn: 中心为零、离散为一的特例是标准正态，表格就是为它印的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: follow a normal distribution, assume a normal distribution, test for normality.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：服从正态分布、假定服从正态分布、做正态性检验。

abstract.en: Picture a hill symmetric on both sides, steepest halfway down and flattening at the edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一座左右对称的山丘，半腰最陡，边缘渐渐变平。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd standing around a fountain, dense at the centre and thinning toward the walls.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人围在喷泉边，中间密，靠墙处渐稀。

abstract.en: Picture a target where most shots fall near the bullseye and only a few reach the outer ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一个靶子，多数弹着点落在靶心附近，只有少数到了外环。

examples.en: The residuals were close to a normal distribution.
examples.cn: 残差接近正态分布。

examples.en: Heights in the sample are normally distributed.
examples.cn: 样本中的身高呈正态分布。

examples.en: To use the table, convert the values to the standard normal distribution.
examples.cn: 要用这张表，先把数值换算成标准正态分布。

dict_mnemonic.text: 前一个词意为「合乎规矩」，后一个词意为「分配」：数值按一种有规律的样式铺开，中间密、两端稀，画出来就是一口钟。

root: 复合术语。normal 出自拉丁 normalis「按曲尺做成的」，词根 norma 指木匠曲尺，更早来源不确定；distribution 出自拉丁 distribuere「分配」＝ dis-（分开）＋ tribuere「分派」，tribuere 一般认为与 tribus「部族」有关。这个短语在十九世纪成形。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe one silhouette: values pile up at the centre and thin out at both ends. The silhouette is then given a probability law, a curve, a standard case, a second name, an error model, a limiting law, a test and, at last, a plain shape for anything that behaves that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述同一个轮廓：数值在中间堆高，两端渐稀。这个轮廓再依次获得概率规律、曲线、标准特例、第二个名称、误差模型、极限规律、一种检验，最后成为任何如此表现之物的朴素形状。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a symmetric hill, highest at the centre and flattening toward both edges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座左右对称的山丘，正中最高，向两侧渐渐变平。

branches.en: THE SHAPE AND THE LAW: the probability rule and the curve drawn from it are one object seen twice.
branches.cn: 形状与规律：概率规则与由它画出的曲线，是同一对象的两种看法。

branches.en: THE SPECIAL CASE: centre zero and spread one make every curve comparable.
branches.cn: 标准特例：中心为零、离散为一，使所有曲线可比。

branches.en: TWO NAMES: an honorific name and a descriptive name point at the same distribution.
branches.cn: 两个名称：纪念性名称与描述性名称指向同一个分布。

branches.en: WHY IT APPEARS: error theory and the summing of independent values both produce this curve.
branches.cn: 为何出现：误差理论与独立数值求和都产生这条曲线。

branches.en: THE TEST AND THE SHAPE: data are checked against it, and any centre-heavy pattern is called by its outline.
branches.cn: 检验与形状：数据要对照它来检查，而任何中间密集的形态都以它的轮廓命名。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin word for a rule and a Latin verb for allotting, so each half can be read with its own family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示「规矩」的拉丁词与一个表示「分派」的拉丁动词接在一起，两半各自可连同词族来读。

latinIntro.en: Latin norma gives normal and normalis; Latin tribuere gives distribute, contribution and tribute.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 norma 给出 normal 与 normalis；拉丁 tribuere 给出 distribute、contribution、tribute。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a standard pattern.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「标准范式」的意思。

items.meaning: made according to a square; regular
items.meaningCN: 按曲尺做成的；合规矩的
items.example: The adjective turns the rule into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词把规矩变成一种性质。

items.example: The normal case is symmetric.
items.exampleCN: 通常的情形是对称的。

items.example: The test checks normality.
items.exampleCN: 这项检验检查正态性。

items.example: Normalize the values first.
items.exampleCN: 先把数值标准化。

items.example: The root supplies the act of handing out.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「分发出去」的动作。

items.example: The verb spreads values across a range.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把数值铺到一个范围里。

items.meaning: the act or result of spreading out
items.example: The distribution is symmetric.
items.exampleCN: 这个分布是对称的。

items.meaning: to give out over a range
items.example: The values distribute around the centre.
items.exampleCN: 数值围绕中心铺开。

latinEntries.meaning: made according to a square, regular
latinEntries.meaningCN: 按曲尺做成的；合规矩的
